title: Bytecode encoding and hot loop density (phase 2)
Convert bytecode storage to Vec<u8> byte stream
description:
Replace `Vec<Instruction>` bytecode storage with `Vec<u8>` byte-stream encoding.

Current state: `crates/lyng-js/bytecode/src/instruction.rs` defines `Instruction` as a Rust enum with three forms (`Abc`, `Abx`, `Ax`). The on-wire encoding via `Instruction::encode_word()` is 4 bytes, but the in-memory `size_of::<Instruction>()` is 8 bytes (discriminant + Ax-form i32 padding, confirmed by mock compile on aarch64-darwin stable Rust).

`crates/lyng-js/bytecode/src/function/template.rs:25` stores `instructions: Vec<Instruction>` on `BytecodeFunction`. `crates/lyng-js/vm/src/vm/dispatch.rs:98-129` per-iteration does `installed.function.instructions().get(i).copied()` — fetching 8 bytes from an arbitrary heap location, matching on the enum discriminant, then matching on the inner opcode.

QuickJS bytecode averages 1.5-2 bytes/op (variable-width byte stream with computed-goto dispatch). V8 Ignition averages similar via accumulator-based ISA with operand-scale prefixes. lyng-js pushes 3-5x more bytecode bytes through the I-cache for the same logical instruction stream.

Goal: Change the storage to `Vec<u8>` carrying the existing 4-byte `Instruction::encode_word()` payload. Keep the logical instruction set unchanged. Decoder reads opcode byte, then operand bytes by opcode-dictated width.

Implementation sketch:
- Replace `instructions: Vec<Instruction>` with `instructions: Vec<u8>` on `BytecodeFunction`.
- Add per-opcode operand-width tables in `lyng_js_bytecode::opcode` (every opcode fits one of the existing 3 forms, so the table is small and constant).
- Rewrite `BytecodeFunctionBuilder` to emit raw bytes; preserve patching APIs (`patch_ax`, `patch_bx`) by writing into known byte positions.
- Rewrite decoder helpers in `bytecode/src/decoder.rs` to advance a cursor by opcode-dictated width.
- Update `vm/src/vm/dispatch.rs` to match on `u8` opcode at the top level (LLVM synthesizes a real jump table for a dense u8 match). Read operand bytes from the byte stream with `unsafe` indexed reads after a one-time bounds check at function entry that proves the stream is well-formed.
- Update `Disassembler` (in `crates/lyng-js/bytecode/src/disassembler.rs`) to walk byte width instead of `Vec<Instruction>`.
- Update `compiler/src/script/emit.rs` and related emit paths to use the new builder.

Related prior work:
- lyng-5u2z (Evaluate compact bytecode encoding for interpreter density, open) — this issue is the implementation; lyng-5u2z's evaluation/design phase is folded into this one. Close lyng-5u2z when this lands.
- lyng-342b (Compact installed bytecode metadata side tables, closed) — orthogonal but adjacent; verify no regressions in metadata layout.
- lyng-26wf (Smi specialization opcodes, closed) — preserve all specialized opcodes added there.

Risk: high blast radius. Touches bytecode IR, compiler emitter, VM decoder, disassembler, and any tooling that reads bytecode. Land as one focused change with full Test262 + density verification, or behind a temporary `bytecode_v2` feature flag if the change is too large to land atomically.
acceptance: All existing `lyng-js-bytecode`, `lyng-js-compiler`, and `lyng-js-vm` tests pass. `cargo run --release -p lyng-js-bench -- density --report /tmp/lyng-js-density-after.md --json /tmp/lyng-js-density-after.json` reports encoded-bytes reductions consistent with going from 8 to 4 bytes per instruction across the executable runtime rows. `cargo run --release -p lyng-js-bench -- compare --report /tmp/compare.md` shows no regression on the synthetic corpus and ideally a measurable improvement on arithmetic-loop (current baseline 5.66ms vs QuickJS 2.91ms; target below 5.0ms after this change in isolation). `cargo run --release -p lyng-js-test262 -- --report /tmp/lyng-js-test262.md -j 12` reports the same pass count as the current whole-suite baseline. `cargo run --release -p lyng-js-bench -- compare --corpus v8-v7 --filter Richards` shows no regression. The dcat handoff records before/after density JSON deltas, compare medians, and Test262 pass counts.

title: Convert bytecode storage to Vec<u8> byte stream
Add short-form opcodes (Jump8, LoadLocal0..3, LoadSmi8)
description:
Add more short-form opcodes building on lyng-26wf.

Current state: lyng-26wf added `LoadZero`, `LoadOne`, `AddSmi`, `SubSmi`, `MulSmi`, `DivSmi`, `ModSmi`, `BitAndSmi`, `EqualZero` (~1% perf improvement on arithmetic-loop). lyng-4zvc added small-arity call opcodes `Call0..3`. Several high-frequency patterns still use the full operand encoding:

- Loop backedges and short conditionals: `Jump`, `JumpIfTrue`, `JumpIfFalse` use the full `Ax` 24-bit signed delta even for loops of <=6 instructions.
- First 4 register accesses: every `Move` from/to registers 0..3 uses the full register operand.
- Small Smi loads: `LoadSmi` encodes i32 even when the value fits in i8 or i16.

QuickJS specialized opcodes (verified from quickjs-opcode.h:290-344): `push_0`, `push_1`, `push_minus1`, `push_i8`, `push_i16`, `get_loc0..3`, `put_loc0..3`, `get_loc8`, `get_loc16`, `if_false8`, `if_true8`, `goto8`, `goto16`. V8 Ignition specialized opcodes: `LdaZero`, `LdaSmi`, `LdaConstant`, `Star0..15`, `JumpIfTrue`/`JumpIfFalse` short forms.

Goal: Add specialized short-form variants of the highest-frequency opcodes. Update the compiler emitter to prefer the narrow form when operands fit. Combined with byte-stream bytecode (1.1), expect 25-40% reduction in average bytes per logical instruction.

Opcodes to add:
- `LoadSmi8 r, i8` — load a small signed integer into a register
- `Jump8 delta`, `JumpIfTrue8 r, delta`, `JumpIfFalse8 r, delta` — 8-bit signed offsets for short backedges and conditionals
- `LoadLocal0..3 dst` — implicit src is register 0..3, only encodes dst (or zero-operand if dst is also a hidden register such as the accumulator-like slot)
- `StoreLocal0..3 src` — implicit dst is register 0..3
- `LoadConst8 r, i8` — single-byte constant pool index for the first 256 constants

Implementation sketch:
- Add opcode variants to `Opcode` (crates/lyng-js/bytecode/src/opcode.rs) and the dispatch table.
- Add per-variant operand widths to the byte-stream encoding tables introduced in 1.1.
- In the compiler emit phase (crates/lyng-js/compiler/src/), add a peephole step or in-emitter selection: prefer `LoadSmi8` when `k in i8::MIN..=i8::MAX`. Same for `Jump*` based on the resolved delta after layout. Same for `Move r, r0..r3` -> `LoadLocal0..3`. Same for `Move r0..r3, r` -> `StoreLocal0..3`.
- Disassembler must understand the new variants.
- Verify `bench density --report` shows real reduction across executable runtime rows.

Related prior work:
- lyng-26wf (Smi specializations, closed) — preserve and extend; do not duplicate
- lyng-4zvc (Small-arity calls, closed) — preserve

Dependencies: lyng-2yow-1.1 (byte stream makes variable widths natural). Can land before 1.1 with full-width operands, but the cache-pressure win comes from the byte stream.
acceptance: `cargo run --release -p lyng-js-bench -- density` shows encoded-bytes reduction across the executable runtime rows vs. the baseline before this change. `cargo run --release -p lyng-js-bench -- runtime --count-opcodes` shows the new short-forms are actually emitted by the compiler for representative workloads — specifically Jump8 / JumpIfFalse8 / LoadLocal0..3 / StoreLocal0..3 appear in the top-20 opcode list for `array-heavy.literal-indexed-runtime` and `class-heavy.runtime`. `cargo test -p lyng-js-bytecode -p lyng-js-compiler -p lyng-js-vm` passes. Test262 conformance unchanged. `compare` shows non-negative change on synthetic compare. The dcat handoff records before/after density JSON deltas and opcode-count distributions for the affected benchmark rows.

title: Add short-form opcodes (Jump8, LoadLocal0..3, LoadSmi8)
Inline IC feedback slot into bytecode operand
description:
Inline the IC feedback slot index into the bytecode operand for feedback-bearing opcodes, removing the parallel `(CodeRef, instruction_offset) -> slot` lookup.

Current state: feedback-bearing opcodes (GetNamedProperty, SetNamedProperty, AssignNamedProperty, StrictAssignNamedProperty, GetKeyedProperty, SetKeyedProperty, AssignKeyedProperty, StrictAssignKeyedProperty, Call0..3, Call, CallMethod, Construct, Add/Sub/Mul/Div/etc, Equal, StrictEqual, LessThan etc, LoadGlobal/StoreGlobal/AssignGlobal, LoadName/AssignName) call `self.record_feedback_site(frame.code(), frame.instruction_offset())` per execution. This is at minimum a map lookup keyed by `(CodeRef, instruction_offset)` to resolve the `FeedbackSlotId`, then another indirection through `Vm::feedback_vectors[code_index]`.

V8 Ignition encodes the slot ID directly in the bytecode operand: `GetNamedProperty acc, recv, name, slot4`. The runtime then does `feedback_vector[slot4]` in one indexed load. JSC LLInt uses a per-bytecode metadata table indexed by bytecode offset — same effect, slot data co-located with bytecode.

Goal: Carry the `FeedbackSlotId` as a bytecode operand on every feedback-bearing opcode. Drop the `(code, instruction_offset) -> slot` lookup in the runtime.

Implementation sketch:
- Extend `Abx` (or define a new `Abxc` 5-byte form post-1.1) to carry the feedback slot index alongside the existing atom/constant operand.
- Compiler already allocates `FeedbackSlotId`s at compile time in `crates/lyng-js/sema`. Emit those IDs as the new operand instead of as a parallel `FeedbackSiteDescriptor`.
- Runtime feedback vector indexing becomes `feedback_vector.slot(slot_id)` directly. Delete the descriptor-site map lookup.
- `crates/lyng-js/bytecode/src/metadata.rs` `feedback_sites: Vec<FeedbackSiteDescriptor>` becomes a documentation/disassembly aid (or remove entirely if no caller needs the reverse mapping).

Related prior work:
- lyng-1xig (Relax poly IC cliff, closed) — preserve the 8-entry polymorphic limit and the shape prefiltering added there
- lyng-46rj (Adaptive named-property dictionary, closed) — orthogonal
- lyng-60hn (Dense indexed-element feedback fast path, closed) — orthogonal

Dependencies: lyng-2yow-1.1 (operand layout cleaner post-byte-stream). May be paired with 1.2 if both touch the encoding generator.
acceptance: Property-access and call hot paths drop one map lookup per execution. Verify via profiler (Instruments / xctrace Time Profiler) that `record_feedback_site` and any feedback-site map lookups are no longer in the per-opcode hot path. Test262 conformance unchanged. `compare` shows improvement on `array-object-loop` (property-access heavy) and `class-heavy.runtime`. `cargo test -p lyng-js-vm -p lyng-js-compiler -p lyng-js-bytecode` passes. The dcat handoff includes a profiler-flamegraph comparison before/after.

description:
Replace the linear-scan polymorphic IC lookup with a hashed or branched data structure. Keep the 8-entry capacity set in lyng-1xig.

Current state: `crates/lyng-js/vm/src/vm/feedback.rs:15` sets `POLYMORPHIC_PROPERTY_CACHE_LIMIT = 8` (raised from 4 in lyng-1xig). The `NamedPropertyFeedback::entries: [Option<NamedPropertyCacheEntry>; 8]` array is scanned linearly via `active_entries()` on every IC lookup. lyng-1xig added receiver-shape prefiltering before full validation, which helps, but the underlying scan is still up to 8 comparisons.

V8's IC uses 4 inline entries with a hashed/sorted-by-shape access pattern; JSC's `StructureStubInfo` similarly. The 8-entry capacity was set to preserve feedback for 4-8 shape sites; lyng-1xig found no measured perf change vs. the previous 4-entry limit (both showed 1.91x QuickJS on polymorphic-property-loop), suggesting the linear scan itself is the limiting factor.

Goal: Improve the polymorphic IC lookup data structure so the per-access cost scales sub-linearly with entry count. Keep the 8-entry capacity. Preserve receiver-shape prefiltering, stale-shape rejection, and invalidation correctness.

Options to evaluate (pick one or compare with measurement):
- Sort entries by `receiver_shape` and do a binary search.
- Hash entries by `receiver_shape & mask` into a 2-way or 4-way set-associative inline cache; fall back to linear scan within a set.
- Unroll the lookup to 8 explicit cmp+branch pairs and let LLVM optimize (already partially the case; verify the codegen).
- Maintain a small (4-element) LRU front cache atop the 8-entry pool — common cases hit the front cache in 1-2 compares.

Implementation sketch:
- Change the `entries` array storage strategy in `NamedPropertyFeedback` and `KeyedPropertyFeedback`.
- Update insert / lookup paths to preserve invalidation epoch tracking.
- Verify cache-state transitions (Uninitialized -> Monomorphic -> Polymorphic -> Megamorphic) work the same; add tests for transitions.
- Re-run the polymorphic-property-loop benchmark added in lyng-1xig.

Related prior work:
- lyng-1xig (Relax IC cliff, closed) — preserve capacity (8); change is the lookup data structure, not the capacity
- lyng-46rj (Adaptive dict, closed) — orthogonal

acceptance: `diagnostics.megamorphic_sites` in the bench JSON does not increase. `diagnostics.live_feedback_sites` unchanged. `cargo run --release -p lyng-js-bench -- compare --filter polymorphic-property-loop` shows non-regression vs. the lyng-1xig baseline of 1.91x QuickJS, with measurable improvement once the cache has 5+ shapes. Hoist frame state into dispatch-loop locals
description:
Hoist immutable-per-activation frame state into the dispatch loop's locals, removing per-opcode `FrameRecord` copies.

Current state: `crates/lyng-js/vm/src/vm/dispatch.rs:99` does `let frame = self.frame().expect(...)` on every iteration. `crates/lyng-js/vm/src/frame.rs:126` defines `FrameRecord` as `Clone + Copy` with 19 fields (`code`, `instruction_offset`, `parameter_initializer_end_offset`, `registers`, `return_register`, `realm`, `lexical_env`, `variable_env`, `this_value`, `construct_this`, `new_target`, `callee`, `tail_caller`, `tail_caller_strict`, `handler_cursor`, `flags`, `kind`, `resume_kind`, `resume_value`, `resume_active`). Estimated size ~88 bytes; copied per opcode.

`installed.function.instructions()` is also re-fetched per iteration (three method calls + a Vec deref) even though it's stable until the frame is replaced.

lyng-3wvk reduced call-frame hot-path overhead at call entry but did not change per-opcode dispatch loop access. This issue is the per-opcode follow-up.

Goal: Refactor the inner dispatch loop so that immutable-per-activation state lives in locals (which LLVM can hoist into registers) and only the genuinely mutable bits (`instruction_offset`, `handler_cursor`, occasionally `lexical_env`, accumulator/resume state) are read/written.

Implementation sketch:
- Split `FrameRecord` semantically into "frame metadata" (stable per activation: `code`, `parameter_initializer_end_offset`, `registers.base`, `registers.len`, `return_register`, `realm`, `variable_env`, `this_value`, `construct_this`, `new_target`, `callee`, `tail_caller`, `tail_caller_strict`, `kind`) and "frame state" (mutable: `instruction_offset`, `handler_cursor`, `lexical_env`, `resume_kind`, `resume_value`, `resume_active`, `flags`).
- In the dispatch outer loop (after Epic 1.1's byte-stream conversion), pick up the frame once per activation and bind locals: `let mut pc: *const u8 = ...; let bytecode_base: *const u8 = ...; let bytecode_end: *const u8 = ...; let register_base: u32 = ...; let installed: &InstalledFunction = ...; let realm = ...; etc.` Only write back to `self.frames` on call, return, throw, or async suspend.
- Pass `&mut FrameState` (small mutable struct) to opcode helpers instead of `FrameRecord`. Reserve `FrameRecord` for cold helpers and debug inspection.
- Preserve rooting, unwinding, for-in/iterator cleanup, and mapped-arguments finalization invariants from lyng-3wvk.

Related prior work:
- lyng-3wvk (Reduce call-frame hot-path size, closed) — call-entry side, this builds on
- lyng-5zky (Eliminate register access bounds checks, closed) — preserves
- lyng-2hhp (Threaded dispatch prototype, closed) — this issue lives inside the new dispatch loop from Epic 3.1

Dependencies: lyng-2yow-1.1 (byte stream — `pc` as `*const u8` is natural). Conceptually independent of 1.2, 1.3, 1.4. Strongly synergistic with Epic 3.1 (the new dispatch loop is the place where the hoisting lives).
acceptance: Per-opcode runtime cost drops. Verified via `bench runtime --preset profile-target` on `array-heavy.iterator-runtime` or `class-heavy.runtime`. Profiler output (`sample` or `xctrace`) confirms `Vm::frame` / `FrameRecord` copying are no longer in the per-opcode hot path. Rooting and unwinding invariants from lyng-3wvk preserved. `cargo test -p lyng-js-vm` passes. Test262 conformance unchanged. `compare` arithmetic-loop and array-object-loop show measurable improvement over the 2026-05-12 baselines. The dcat handoff includes a flamegraph comparison and per-opcode cycle-count estimate.

Object storage layout: inline slots and unified metadata (phase 2)
description:
Second-phase object-storage epic on top of lyng-4dwr.

The third-party engine comparison (lyng-js vs QuickJS, V8, JSC) finds that lyng-js named-property access on the hit path requires 3+ chained dereferences vs. 1-2 in the comparison engines:

1. ObjectRef -> `Vec<Option<ObjectMetadata>>` (bounds check + Option discrimination)
2. ObjectMetadata -> `named_slots: Option<NamedSlotStorageRef>` (Option discrimination)
3. NamedSlotStorageRef -> GC slot array (handle dereference)
4. Slot array indexed at `shape.slot_offset`

V8: Map check + single indexed load on the object header (inline properties), overflow to PropertyArray for the rare cold case.

JSC: butterfly pattern. Object header has inline slots forward; an attached butterfly carries out-of-line slots and array elements backward. One indexed load past the object header.

QuickJS: `JSProperty[]` lives directly in the object record; the shape hash table is co-located with `JSShape` in memory. Two loads.

lyng-js side-table architecture is elegant for memory analytics and the typed allocation domains in lyng-js-gc, but pays for the flexibility on every property access. The 10+ parallel `Vec<Option<T>>` arrays in `ObjectRuntime` (`object_metadata`, `class_records`, `module_namespaces`, `maps`, `sets`, `array_buffers`, `data_views`, `typed_arrays`, `temporal_objects`, `regexp_payloads`, `generator_states`, `shape_metadata`) keyed by object index also mean any object-kind-specific code does `vec.get(index).as_ref()` per access.

This epic collapses object access to "shape compare + one indexed load past the object header" for the monomorphic case, with three sub-issues:

- 2.1 Fold the 10+ object-kind side tables into one unified `ObjectMetadata` struct with a cold `Option<ObjectKindPayload>` enum for rare kinds (typed arrays, data views, temporal, regexp, generators, maps, sets, module namespaces, class records).
- 2.2 Inline first N named slots into the object record so monomorphic property access is one indexed load past the header (parallels V8's in-object properties / JSC's butterfly inline section). N=4 matches `SMALL_SHAPE_INLINE_PROPERTY_LIMIT`.
- 2.3 Drop `Vec<Option<FeedbackVector>>` for `Vec<FeedbackVector>` with a default "empty" sentinel; the Option is only meaningful before warmup, and warmup state can live in the vector itself.

Related prior work: lyng-342b (Compact installed bytecode metadata side tables, closed) — different scope (bytecode metadata, not object metadata) but same architectural intent.

Sources:
- Third-party engine analysis: /tmp/lyng-js-engine-analysis.md (in-session)
- Existing perf epic: lyng-4dwr
acceptance: All three sub-issues land with measured before/after evidence in their dcat handoffs. The combined compare-corpus median on array-object-loop and class-heavy.runtime shows measurable improvement vs. the 2026-05-12 baselines. The runtime accounting snapshots in reports/js/lyng-js/bench.md show reduced heap reserved bytes for typical monomorphic-property workloads. Test262 pass count remains unchanged. GC tracing and rooting correctness verified by existing tests plus targeted lyng-js-gc coverage. Profiler evidence shows the property-access hot path drops at least one cache miss per access on monomorphic sites.

title: Object storage layout: inline slots and unified metadata (phase 2)
Unify object-kind side tables into one ObjectMetadata
description:
Fold the 10+ object-kind side tables in `ObjectRuntime` into a single unified `ObjectMetadata` struct with a cold `Option<ObjectKindPayload>` enum for rare kinds.

Current state: `crates/lyng-js/objects/src/runtime.rs` `ObjectRuntime` has these parallel `Vec<Option<T>>` arrays, all keyed by object index:
- `object_metadata: Vec<Option<ObjectMetadata>>`
- `class_records: Vec<Option<ClassRecord>>`
- `module_namespaces: Vec<Option<ModuleNamespaceObject>>`
- `maps: Vec<Option<MapObjectData>>`
- `sets: Vec<Option<SetObjectData>>`
- `array_buffers: Vec<Option<ArrayBufferObjectData>>`
- `data_views: Vec<Option<DataViewObjectData>>`
- `typed_arrays: Vec<Option<TypedArrayObjectData>>`
- `temporal_objects: Vec<Option<TemporalObjectData>>`
- `regexp_payloads: Vec<Option<RegExpPayload>>`
- `generator_states: Vec<Option<GeneratorState>>`
- `shape_metadata: Vec<Option<ShapeMetadata>>`

`crates/lyng-js/objects/src/runtime_storage.rs:21-220` defines accessors for each: `map_slot()`, `typed_array_slot()`, `regexp_payload_slot()`, etc. Every access does `vec.get(object_index(id)).as_ref()` (or `.copied().flatten()`), incurring bounds check + Option discrimination per access. Most objects use only `object_metadata` plus zero or one of the type-specific tables, so the remaining 9 tables are wasted memory and dispatch indirection.

Goal: Move per-object payload into a single struct stored in one contiguous `Vec<ObjectMetadata>` (no `Option` — invalid IDs trap explicitly). The struct contains the common fields inline plus a cold `payload: Option<ObjectKindPayload>` enum carrying the rare type-specific data.

Implementation sketch:
- Define `ObjectKindPayload` as an enum with variants for each current side table: `Map(Box<MapObjectData>)`, `Set(Box<SetObjectData>)`, `ArrayBuffer(ArrayBufferObjectData)`, `DataView(DataViewObjectData)`, `TypedArray(Box<TypedArrayObjectData>)`, `Temporal(TemporalObjectData)`, `RegExp(Box<RegExpPayload>)`, `Generator(GeneratorState)`, `ClassRecord(Box<ClassRecord>)`, `ModuleNamespace(Box<ModuleNamespaceObject>)`. Box the larger variants so the enum stays small (target <=32 bytes).
- Replace the 10 parallel `Vec<Option<T>>` arrays with one `Vec<ObjectMetadata>` where `ObjectMetadata` carries `shape: ShapeId`, `flags: ObjectFlags`, `prototype: Option<ObjectRef>`, `named_slots: Option<NamedSlotStorageRef>`, `elements: Option<ElementStorageRef>`, `payload: Option<ObjectKindPayload>`, `last_invalidation: Option<InvalidationEvent>`.
- Rewrite all `Self::map_slot(...)`, `Self::typed_array_slot(...)`, etc. accessors to read through the unified payload (pattern match on the enum).
- `ShapeMetadata` may stay separate since it's keyed by `ShapeId` not `ObjectRef`, but verify whether a single `Vec<ShapeMetadata>` indexed by `shape_index(id)` makes sense too.
- GC tracing updated to walk the unified storage.

Related prior work:
- lyng-342b (Compact installed bytecode metadata side tables, closed) — same architectural intent, different scope (bytecode metadata not object metadata)
- lyng-62fh (Include VM-owned residency in runtime memory accounting, closed) — preserve memory accounting hooks
- lyng-4se9 (Inline small shape transition cache, closed) — preserve

Risk: medium — touches every place that reads object-kind data. Mitigation: introduce unified `ObjectMetadata` alongside the side tables first, migrate kind-by-kind, delete the side table once all callers move. Land as a series of small commits.
acceptance: Memory accounting snapshots (`runtime.spec-bootstrap` and friends in `reports/js/lyng-js/bench.md`) show reduced heap reserved bytes for typical workloads — concretely, the per-object reserved overhead drops by the size of the 9+ retired side tables for objects that don't use those kinds. Test262 conformance unchanged. `compare` and `runtime` benchmarks show non-regression and ideally a small improvement on `class-heavy.runtime`. GC tracing tests pass. `cargo test -p lyng-js-objects -p lyng-js-vm -p lyng-js-tests` passes. The dcat handoff records memory-snapshot deltas and a flamegraph showing the object-kind dispatch hot path post-change.

Inline first N named slots into the object record
description:
Inline the first N named slots into the object record so the monomorphic property-access fast path is one indexed load past the object header.

Current state: Named properties live in a separate GC-managed slot array referenced from `ObjectMetadata` via `NamedSlotStorageRef`. The hot path after shape compare succeeds is:

1. Load `ObjectMetadata` (after Epic 2.1 this is one indexed load)
2. Load `named_slots: Option<NamedSlotStorageRef>` from metadata
3. Dereference `NamedSlotStorageRef` into the GC slot array
4. Index into slot array at `shape.slot_offset`

V8 puts the first N (typically 2 on 64-bit, 3 on 32-bit) properties inline in the object header. The IC's slot_offset tells you which location it is — inline slot N or out-of-line offset M. Either way, one indexed load past the header.

JSC's butterfly: object header has inline slots forward; an attached butterfly carries out-of-line slots and array elements backward. Same fast path: one indexed load.

`crates/lyng-js/objects/src/shapes.rs:17` defines `SMALL_SHAPE_INLINE_PROPERTY_LIMIT = 4`, matching the inline-property concept already in the shape design. Today that constant controls when the shape switches from inline descriptor scan to a flattened lookup table — it does not control whether the named slot storage itself is inline.

Goal: Add `inline_slots: [Value; 4]` to `ObjectMetadata` (or the equivalent post-Epic 2.1 unified struct). Shape descriptors mark each slot as inline (one of 4 inline positions) or out-of-line (offset into the heap-allocated named slot array). The IC fast path becomes a single indexed load from the object record for shapes whose properties all fit inline.

Implementation sketch:
- N=4 matches `SMALL_SHAPE_INLINE_PROPERTY_LIMIT` — most objects have all properties inline.
- Add `inline_slots: [Value; 4]` to the unified `ObjectMetadata` from Epic 2.1.
- Extend `ShapeProperty` (or the IC cache entry from Epic 1.3) to record whether each slot is inline or out-of-line. Encoding: high bit of `slot_offset` distinguishes inline (0b1xxx) from out-of-line (0b0xxx).
- IC entry stores the slot kind alongside the offset. The dispatch chooses the appropriate load via a single branch.
- Compiler/runtime path that allocates new named slots arrays only does so when shape transitions past 4 properties.
- GC tracing updates: trace inline_slots as part of `ObjectMetadata` tracing.
- Preserve `NamedPropertyStorageMode::Dictionary` fallback semantics for irregular objects.

Related prior work:
- lyng-4se9 (Inline small shape transition cache, closed) — preserves
- lyng-46rj (Adaptive named-property dictionary, closed) — preserves
- lyng-1xig (Relax poly IC cliff, closed) — IC entry size grows slightly; verify cache line fit

Dependencies: lyng-3bxz-2.1 (cleaner inside the unified `ObjectMetadata`). Synergistic with Epic 1.3 (IC slot in operand) — the IC entry needs the inline/out-of-line bit.

Risk: high — touches the object layout, GC tracing, IC entries, shape transition logic. Land behind a feature flag if possible.
acceptance: Hot property-access workloads (`array-object-loop`, `class-heavy.runtime`) show measurable improvement over the 2026-05-12 baselines. Test262 conformance unchanged. `cargo test -p lyng-js-objects -p lyng-js-vm -p lyng-js-tests` passes. GC tracing tests pass. Memory accounting shows reduced live bytes for monomorphic small objects (no separate named-slot allocation for <=4 properties). Profiler evidence shows the property-access hot path drops one heap dereference per access on monomorphic sites. The dcat handoff records before/after benchmark medians, memory snapshots, and a flamegraph diff.

Drop Vec<Option<FeedbackVector>> for direct storage
description:
Drop `Vec<Option<FeedbackVector>>` for `Vec<FeedbackVector>` with a default "empty" sentinel; eliminate per-access Option discrimination on the IC hot path.

Current state: `crates/lyng-js/vm/src/vm.rs:187-188` defines `feedback_vectors: Vec<Option<FeedbackVector>>` keyed by `CodeRef` index. Every feedback-bearing opcode pays a bounds check + `Option` discrimination per execution.

The `Option` is only meaningful before the warmup threshold fires (`FEEDBACK_ALLOCATION_THRESHOLD = 2` in feedback.rs:14); once a feedback vector is allocated for a `CodeRef`, it stays allocated until uninstall (rare).

Goal: Replace `Vec<Option<FeedbackVector>>` with `Vec<FeedbackVector>` where the default-constructed `FeedbackVector` is the equivalent of "uninitialized" (zero slots, zero allocated bytes, state `FeedbackInlineCacheState::Uninitialized`). The warmup threshold logic moves into a counter on the vector itself.

Implementation sketch:
- `FeedbackVector::empty()` returns a sentinel that allocates no slot storage but answers `slot_count() == 0` and treats all reads as `FeedbackInlineCacheState::Uninitialized`. Internally this is a vector with `entries: Vec::new()` and an inline `warmup_counter: u16`.
- Replace `feedback_vectors: Vec<Option<FeedbackVector>>` with `Vec<FeedbackVector>`; resize_with `FeedbackVector::empty`.
- The inline IC check becomes one indexed load + state check, no `Option` discrimination.
- `Vm::feedback_warmup: Vec<u16>` folds into `FeedbackVector::warmup_counter`. Remove the parallel `feedback_warmup` vector.
- Existing snapshot APIs (`FeedbackVectorFootprint`, `FeedbackVectorSnapshot`) must continue to work; they already handle the "no slots allocated" case.

Related prior work:
- lyng-1xig (Relax IC cliff, closed) — preserves
- lyng-60hn (Dense indexed-element feedback fast path, closed) — preserves
- lyng-ws94 (Harden feedback vectors and inline-cache data, closed) — preserves invariants

Dependencies: lyng-2fon (1.3, slot-id-in-operand) makes this cleaner because the indexing becomes `vectors[code_index].slot(slot_id)` directly. Independent of Epic 2.1 and 2.2 in code, but spirit-matched with this epic (eliminating Option-laden side tables).
acceptance: IC fast path drops one branch per execution (verify via profiler / cargo asm). No regression in feedback warmup behavior; `bench runtime` shows the same warmup distribution. Memory accounting unchanged on cold runtime; ideally slight reduction on warm runtime (one less Option discriminant per allocated vector). Test262 conformance unchanged. `cargo test -p lyng-js-vm` passes. The dcat handoff records before/after IC fast-path cycle estimates.

VM dispatch: single-loop and direct-threaded (phase 2)
description:
Second-phase dispatch epic that finishes what lyng-2hhp started.

lyng-2hhp prototyped a function-pointer threaded dispatch mode (`VmDispatchMode::FunctionTable`) parallel to the existing match-based dispatch. The result was effectively neutral on arithmetic-loop (7.805ms match mode vs 7.809ms function-table mode) and stayed behind a switch.

The third-party engine comparison identifies why the function-table prototype didn't pay off: every threaded handler returns `Result<ThreadedStep, _>` with a `SwitchToMatch` variant, and any opcode without a specialized threaded handler triggers a return-and-restart in match mode. Worst-of-both-worlds: function-call boundary per opcode plus state-check overhead, plus the match dispatch is still in the binary.

V8 jitless: precompiled-to-native bytecode handlers embedded in the binary, dispatched via `jmp *[table + opcode*8]` with no C-loop. JSC LLInt: handlers hand-written in offlineasm and assembled at build time, direct-threaded dispatch with no C-loop. Both achieve interpreter-only performance that the function-pointer-with-fallback approach cannot match.

Two paths for lyng-js on stable Rust:

3.1 (this epic, primary): Single dispatch loop with a top-level `match opcode_byte` on `u8`, every opcode handler `#[inline(always)]` inline in the loop, no fallback to a parallel dispatch mode. LLVM synthesizes a real jump table for a dense u8 match. This needs the byte-stream bytecode from Epic 1 (1.1) — once `Instruction` is `u8` not an enum, the outer match becomes a contiguous jump-table-friendly match.

3.2 (optional, backlog): Once Rust's `become` (guaranteed tail call) stabilizes, convert to true direct-threaded dispatch via a `static DISPATCH_TABLE: [extern "rust-call" fn(&mut DispatchState) -> !; OPCODE_COUNT]` where each handler decodes its own operands and tail-calls the next handler via the table. Expected ~10-20% over jump-table-match.

Hoisting hot frame state into the dispatch loop's locals (lyng-3wvk continuation) belongs here rather than under Epic 1 because the win materializes inside the new dispatch loop — current per-iteration `self.frame().expect(...)` copies an ~88-byte FrameRecord that should be stable across the inner loop except for `instruction_offset` and a few other mutable bits.

Related prior work:
- lyng-2hhp (Prototype threaded VM dispatch, closed, neutral) — supersedes
- lyng-3wvk (Reduce call-frame hot-path size, closed) — builds on
- lyng-5zky (Eliminate validated VM register access bounds checks, closed) — builds on

Sources:
- Third-party engine analysis: /tmp/lyng-js-engine-analysis.md (in-session)
- Existing perf epic: lyng-4dwr
acceptance: Both sub-issues (3.1 mandatory, 3.2 backlog/optional) addressed with measured evidence. The `VmDispatchMode::FunctionTable` mode and `ThreadedStep::SwitchToMatch` are removed; only one dispatch loop remains. Profiler evidence on arithmetic-loop shows a measurable IPC improvement vs. the 2026-05-12 baseline of 5.66ms (target: below 4.5ms median, ideally below 4.0ms post Epic 1). Test262 pass count unchanged. Hot frame state hoisting verified by profiler — `FrameRecord` copy is no longer in the per-opcode hot path.

title: VM dispatch: single-loop and direct-threaded (phase 2)
Single-loop opcode dispatch with no SwitchToMatch fallback
description:
Replace the current dual `match`-dispatch / `FunctionTable`-dispatch design with a single dispatch loop that has no fallback. Finishes what lyng-2hhp prototyped.

Current state: `crates/lyng-js/vm/src/vm/dispatch.rs` has two dispatch modes:

- `VmDispatchMode::Match` (default): a single 1500-line `run_match` function with a top-level `match instruction` (on `Instruction::{Abc, Abx, Ax}`) and a nested `match opcode`.
- `VmDispatchMode::FunctionTable` (lyng-2hhp): a fn-pointer-dispatched threaded mode. Every threaded handler returns `Result<ThreadedStep, _>` where `ThreadedStep::SwitchToMatch` causes the loop to abandon threading and restart in match mode for any opcode without a specialized threaded handler. lyng-2hhp benchmark result was neutral (7.805ms match vs 7.809ms function-table on arithmetic-loop), and the mode stayed behind a switch.

The reason FunctionTable did not pay off: every threaded handler has a function-call boundary, a `Result` discriminant check, and the fallback restart logic. The match dispatch is also still in the binary. Worst-of-both-worlds.

V8 jitless and JSC LLInt both use direct-threaded dispatch with no C-loop. On stable Rust, the closest portable approximation is a single `loop { match opcode_byte { 0 => handler_0, ... } }` where each handler `#[inline(always)]`s the work, decodes its own operands from a local `pc: *const u8`, and `continue`s. LLVM synthesizes a real jump table for a dense `u8` match — within ~10-20% of true computed-goto.

Goal: Replace both today's dispatch modes with a single new `run` function that:

- Reads from `Vec<u8>` bytecode (post Epic 1.1 / lyng-5r8r).
- Top-level matches on `u8` opcode at the byte level.
- Each arm is `#[inline(always)]` work that updates local `pc`, decodes operands, executes, and `continue`s the loop.
- Calls into `lyng-js-ops` helpers for the semantic step; those helpers should inline under LTO. Confirm LTO is enabled in the release profile.
- Keeps dispatch counters (`opcode_dispatch_counts`) and debugger polling behind const-generic specialization, same as today's `run_match::<COUNT_OPCODES, DEBUG>` — the no-debug, no-count path stays branch-free.
- Hoists hot frame state into locals (this work is the partner of lyng-ofuh / 1.5).

Implementation sketch:
- Delete `VmDispatchMode::FunctionTable`, `run_function_table`, and the per-handler `ThreadedOpcodeHandler` fn-pointer table.
- Delete `ThreadedStep::SwitchToMatch` and the inner step return type.
- Rewrite `run_match` as the unified `run` function with the structure above.
- Keep `VmDispatchMode` if there's value in retaining an env switch for debugging (e.g. force-disable-jump-table-codegen for profiler triage), but document it as a debug-only knob; otherwise delete it entirely.
- Verify LLVM jump-table codegen via `cargo asm` or Godbolt-style assembly inspection on the final hot loop. If LLVM doesn't synthesize the table, fall back to an explicit `static HANDLERS: [fn(...); OPCODE_COUNT]` table without the `SwitchToMatch` complication.

Related prior work:
- lyng-2hhp (Prototype threaded VM dispatch, closed, neutral) — supersedes
- lyng-5zky (Eliminate validated VM register access bounds checks, closed) — preserves
- lyng-3wvk (Reduce call-frame hot-path size, closed) — preserves

Dependencies: lyng-5r8r (Epic 1.1, byte stream) — strict. Without byte stream, the inner match is on `Instruction` and LLVM is less likely to synthesize a jump table. lyng-ofuh (Epic 1.5, hoist frame state) — synergistic; either lands together or 1.5 first then 3.1 builds on it.
acceptance: Hot loops show improved IPC (instructions per cycle) under perf monitoring (Instruments / xctrace). `compare` arithmetic-loop drops below 4.5ms median, ideally below 4.0ms when stacked with Epic 1 (current baseline 5.66ms, QuickJS 2.91ms). All existing tests pass; Test262 conformance unchanged. Code surface area decreases — one dispatch loop instead of two. `VmDispatchMode::FunctionTable` and `ThreadedStep::SwitchToMatch` are removed (or `VmDispatchMode` is retained only as a debug-only knob, clearly documented). Cargo asm or compiler explorer evidence that LLVM emits a jump table for the top-level opcode match. The dcat handoff records before/after compare medians, Test262 pass count, and the codegen evidence.

Direct-threaded dispatch via guaranteed tail calls
description:
Optional / backlog: convert dispatch to true direct-threaded via guaranteed tail calls once Rust's `become` keyword stabilizes (or behind a nightly cfg).

Context: After Epic 3.1 (single dispatch loop with `match opcode_byte`), the LLVM-synthesized jump table covers ~80% of the way to true computed-goto. The remaining ~10-20% is achievable when every opcode handler tail-calls the next handler directly, skipping the loop entry / state-fetch overhead. This is exactly what JSC LLInt does in offlineasm and V8's precompiled Ignition handlers do at the machine level.

On stable Rust today, `become` (guaranteed tail call) is unstable. There is no portable way to express true direct-threaded dispatch in safe Rust without it. The C `goto *table[op]` idiom does not have a direct safe-Rust analog.

Goal: Once `become` stabilizes (or behind an `unstable_become` nightly cfg), implement the dispatch loop as a table of tail-call handlers.

Implementation sketch (when feasible):
- Define `DispatchHandler = extern "rust-call" fn(&mut DispatchState) -> !`.
- Build `static DISPATCH_TABLE: [DispatchHandler; OPCODE_COUNT]`.
- Each handler:
  - Decodes its operands from `state.pc` directly.
  - Updates `state.pc` past its operand bytes.

description.new:
Optional / backlog: convert dispatch to true direct-threaded via guaranteed tail calls once Rust's `become` keyword stabilizes (or behind a nightly cfg).

Context: After Epic 3.1 (single dispatch loop with `match opcode_byte`), the LLVM-synthesized jump table covers ~80% of the way to true computed-goto. The remaining ~10-20% is achievable when every opcode handler tail-calls the next handler directly, skipping the loop entry / state-fetch overhead. This is exactly what JSC LLInt does in offlineasm and V8's precompiled Ignition handlers do at the machine level.

On stable Rust today, `become` (guaranteed tail call) is unstable. There is no portable way to express true direct-threaded dispatch in safe Rust without it. The C `goto *table[op]` idiom does not have a direct safe-Rust analog.

Goal: Once `become` stabilizes (or behind an `unstable_become` nightly cfg), implement the dispatch loop as a table of tail-call handlers.

Implementation sketch (when feasible):
- Define `DispatchHandler = extern "rust-call" fn(&mut DispatchState) -> !`.
- Build `static DISPATCH_TABLE: [DispatchHandler; OPCODE_COUNT]`.
- Each handler:
  - Decodes its operands from `state.pc` directly.
  - Updates `state.pc` past its operand bytes.
  - Executes the semantic step (possibly inlining `lyng-js-ops` helpers).
  - Loads next opcode byte; `become DISPATCH_TABLE[opcode](state)`.
- Treat as feature-gated under `#[cfg(feature = "tail_call_dispatch")]` while the keyword is unstable. Default builds use Epic 3.1's match-jump-table dispatch.

Alternative path if `become` stabilization is delayed indefinitely:
- Write the dispatch loop in a single function with `#[inline(never)]` handler labels and a `goto`-style match. Accept that LLVM jump-table generation from Epic 3.1 does most of the work.
- In that case this issue can be closed without action.

title: Design ECMA-402 architecture and verification workflow
Convert bytecode storage to Vec<u8> byte stream
description:
Replace `Vec<Instruction>` bytecode storage with `Vec<u8>` byte-stream encoding.

Current state: `crates/lyng-js/bytecode/src/instruction.rs` defines `Instruction` as a Rust enum with three forms (`Abc`, `Abx`, `Ax`). The on-wire encoding via `Instruction::encode_word()` is 4 bytes, but the in-memory `size_of::<Instruction>()` is 8 bytes (discriminant + Ax-form i32 padding, confirmed by mock compile on aarch64-darwin stable Rust).

`crates/lyng-js/bytecode/src/function/template.rs:25` stores `instructions: Vec<Instruction>` on `BytecodeFunction`. `crates/lyng-js/vm/src/vm/dispatch.rs:98-129` per-iteration does `installed.function.instructions().get(i).copied()` — fetching 8 bytes from an arbitrary heap location, matching on the enum discriminant, then matching on the inner opcode.

QuickJS bytecode averages 1.5-2 bytes/op (variable-width byte stream with computed-goto dispatch). V8 Ignition averages similar via accumulator-based ISA with operand-scale prefixes. lyng-js pushes 3-5x more bytecode bytes through the I-cache for the same logical instruction stream.

Goal: Change the storage to `Vec<u8>` carrying the existing 4-byte `Instruction::encode_word()` payload. Keep the logical instruction set unchanged. Decoder reads opcode byte, then operand bytes by opcode-dictated width.

Implementation sketch:
- Replace `instructions: Vec<Instruction>` with `instructions: Vec<u8>` on `BytecodeFunction`.
- Add per-opcode operand-width tables in `lyng_js_bytecode::opcode` (every opcode fits one of the existing 3 forms, so the table is small and constant).
- Rewrite `BytecodeFunctionBuilder` to emit raw bytes; preserve patching APIs (`patch_ax`, `patch_bx`) by writing into known byte positions.
- Rewrite decoder helpers in `bytecode/src/decoder.rs` to advance a cursor by opcode-dictated width.
- Update `vm/src/vm/dispatch.rs` to match on `u8` opcode at the top level (LLVM synthesizes a real jump table for a dense u8 match). Read operand bytes from the byte stream with `unsafe` indexed reads after a one-time bounds check at function entry that proves the stream is well-formed.
- Update `Disassembler` (in `crates/lyng-js/bytecode/src/disassembler.rs`) to walk byte width instead of `Vec<Instruction>`.
- Update `compiler/src/script/emit.rs` and related emit paths to use the new builder.

Related prior work:
- lyng-5u2z (Evaluate compact bytecode encoding for interpreter density, open) — this issue is the implementation; lyng-5u2z's evaluation/design phase is folded into this one. Close lyng-5u2z when this lands.
- lyng-342b (Compact installed bytecode metadata side tables, closed) — orthogonal but adjacent; verify no regressions in metadata layout.
- lyng-26wf (Smi specialization opcodes, closed) — preserve all specialized opcodes added there.

Risk: high blast radius. Touches bytecode IR, compiler emitter, VM decoder, disassembler, and any tooling that reads bytecode. Land as one focused change with full Test262 + density verification, or behind a temporary `bytecode_v2` feature flag if the change is too large to land atomically.
acceptance: All existing `lyng-js-bytecode`, `lyng-js-compiler`, and `lyng-js-vm` tests pass. `cargo run --release -p lyng-js-bench -- density --report /tmp/lyng-js-density-after.md --json /tmp/lyng-js-density-after.json` reports encoded-bytes reductions consistent with going from 8 to 4 bytes per instruction across the executable runtime rows. `cargo run --release -p lyng-js-bench -- compare --report /tmp/compare.md` shows no regression on the synthetic corpus and ideally a measurable improvement on arithmetic-loop (current baseline 5.66ms vs QuickJS 2.91ms; target below 5.0ms after this change in isolation). `cargo run --release -p lyng-js-test262 -- --report /tmp/lyng-js-test262.md -j 12` reports the same pass count as the current whole-suite baseline. `cargo run --release -p lyng-js-bench -- compare --corpus v8-v7 --filter Richards` shows no regression. The dcat handoff records before/after density JSON deltas, compare medians, and Test262 pass counts.

Add short-form opcodes (Jump8, LoadLocal0..3, LoadSmi8)
description:
Add more short-form opcodes building on lyng-26wf.

Current state: lyng-26wf added `LoadZero`, `LoadOne`, `AddSmi`, `SubSmi`, `MulSmi`, `DivSmi`, `ModSmi`, `BitAndSmi`, `EqualZero` (~1% perf improvement on arithmetic-loop). lyng-4zvc added small-arity call opcodes `Call0..3`. Several high-frequency patterns still use the full operand encoding:

- Loop backedges and short conditionals: `Jump`, `JumpIfTrue`, `JumpIfFalse` use the full `Ax` 24-bit signed delta even for loops of <=6 instructions.
- First 4 register accesses: every `Move` from/to registers 0..3 uses the full register operand.
- Small Smi loads: `LoadSmi` encodes i32 even when the value fits in i8 or i16.

QuickJS specialized opcodes (verified from quickjs-opcode.h:290-344): `push_0`, `push_1`, `push_minus1`, `push_i8`, `push_i16`, `get_loc0..3`, `put_loc0..3`, `get_loc8`, `get_loc16`, `if_false8`, `if_true8`, `goto8`, `goto16`. V8 Ignition specialized opcodes: `LdaZero`, `LdaSmi`, `LdaConstant`, `Star0..15`, `JumpIfTrue`/`JumpIfFalse` short forms.

Goal: Add specialized short-form variants of the highest-frequency opcodes. Update the compiler emitter to prefer the narrow form when operands fit. Combined with byte-stream bytecode (1.1), expect 25-40% reduction in average bytes per logical instruction.

Opcodes to add:
- `LoadSmi8 r, i8` — load a small signed integer into a register
- `Jump8 delta`, `JumpIfTrue8 r, delta`, `JumpIfFalse8 r, delta` — 8-bit signed offsets for short backedges and conditionals
- `LoadLocal0..3 dst` — implicit src is register 0..3, only encodes dst (or zero-operand if dst is also a hidden register such as the accumulator-like slot)
- `StoreLocal0..3 src` — implicit dst is register 0..3
- `LoadConst8 r, i8` — single-byte constant pool index for the first 256 constants

Implementation sketch:
- Add opcode variants to `Opcode` (crates/lyng-js/bytecode/src/opcode.rs) and the dispatch table.
- Add per-variant operand widths to the byte-stream encoding tables introduced in 1.1.
- In the compiler emit phase (crates/lyng-js/compiler/src/), add a peephole step or in-emitter selection: prefer `LoadSmi8` when `k in i8::MIN..=i8::MAX`. Same for `Jump*` based on the resolved delta after layout. Same for `Move r, r0..r3` -> `LoadLocal0..3`. Same for `Move r0..r3, r` -> `StoreLocal0..3`.
- Disassembler must understand the new variants.
- Verify `bench density --report` shows real reduction across executable runtime rows.

Related prior work:
- lyng-26wf (Smi specializations, closed) — preserve and extend; do not duplicate
- lyng-4zvc (Small-arity calls, closed) — preserve

Dependencies: lyng-2yow-1.1 (byte stream makes variable widths natural). Can land before 1.1 with full-width operands, but the cache-pressure win comes from the byte stream.
acceptance: `cargo run --release -p lyng-js-bench -- density` shows encoded-bytes reduction across the executable runtime rows vs. the baseline before this change. `cargo run --release -p lyng-js-bench -- runtime --count-opcodes` shows the new short-forms are actually emitted by the compiler for representative workloads — specifically Jump8 / JumpIfFalse8 / LoadLocal0..3 / StoreLocal0..3 appear in the top-20 opcode list for `array-heavy.literal-indexed-runtime` and `class-heavy.runtime`. `cargo test -p lyng-js-bytecode -p lyng-js-compiler -p lyng-js-vm` passes. Test262 conformance unchanged. `compare` shows non-negative change on synthetic compare. The dcat handoff records before/after density JSON deltas and opcode-count distributions for the affected benchmark rows.

title: Add short-form opcodes (Jump8, LoadLocal0..3, LoadSmi8)
Inline IC feedback slot into bytecode operand
description:
Inline the IC feedback slot index into the bytecode operand for feedback-bearing opcodes, removing the parallel `(CodeRef, instruction_offset) -> slot` lookup.

Current state: feedback-bearing opcodes (GetNamedProperty, SetNamedProperty, AssignNamedProperty, StrictAssignNamedProperty, GetKeyedProperty, SetKeyedProperty, AssignKeyedProperty, StrictAssignKeyedProperty, Call0..3, Call, CallMethod, Construct, Add/Sub/Mul/Div/etc, Equal, StrictEqual, LessThan etc, LoadGlobal/StoreGlobal/AssignGlobal, LoadName/AssignName) call `self.record_feedback_site(frame.code(), frame.instruction_offset())` per execution. This is at minimum a map lookup keyed by `(CodeRef, instruction_offset)` to resolve the `FeedbackSlotId`, then another indirection through `Vm::feedback_vectors[code_index]`.

V8 Ignition encodes the slot ID directly in the bytecode operand: `GetNamedProperty acc, recv, name, slot4`. The runtime then does `feedback_vector[slot4]` in one indexed load. JSC LLInt uses a per-bytecode metadata table indexed by bytecode offset — same effect, slot data co-located with bytecode.

Goal: Carry the `FeedbackSlotId` as a bytecode operand on every feedback-bearing opcode. Drop the `(code, instruction_offset) -> slot` lookup in the runtime.

Implementation sketch:
- Extend `Abx` (or define a new `Abxc` 5-byte form post-1.1) to carry the feedback slot index alongside the existing atom/constant operand.
- Compiler already allocates `FeedbackSlotId`s at compile time in `crates/lyng-js/sema`. Emit those IDs as the new operand instead of as a parallel `FeedbackSiteDescriptor`.
- Runtime feedback vector indexing becomes `feedback_vector.slot(slot_id)` directly. Delete the descriptor-site map lookup.
- `crates/lyng-js/bytecode/src/metadata.rs` `feedback_sites: Vec<FeedbackSiteDescriptor>` becomes a documentation/disassembly aid (or remove entirely if no caller needs the reverse mapping).

Related prior work:
- lyng-1xig (Relax poly IC cliff, closed) — preserve the 8-entry polymorphic limit and the shape prefiltering added there
- lyng-46rj (Adaptive named-property dictionary, closed) — orthogonal
- lyng-60hn (Dense indexed-element feedback fast path, closed) — orthogonal

Dependencies: lyng-2yow-1.1 (operand layout cleaner post-byte-stream). May be paired with 1.2 if both touch the encoding generator.
acceptance: Property-access and call hot paths drop one map lookup per execution. Verify via profiler (Instruments / xctrace Time Profiler) that `record_feedback_site` and any feedback-site map lookups are no longer in the per-opcode hot path. Test262 conformance unchanged. `compare` shows improvement on `array-object-loop` (property-access heavy) and `class-heavy.runtime`. `cargo test -p lyng-js-vm -p lyng-js-compiler -p lyng-js-bytecode` passes. The dcat handoff includes a profiler-flamegraph comparison before/after.

title: Inline IC feedback slot into bytecode operand
Hoist frame state into dispatch-loop locals
description:
Hoist immutable-per-activation frame state into the dispatch loop's locals, removing per-opcode `FrameRecord` copies.

Current state: `crates/lyng-js/vm/src/vm/dispatch.rs:99` does `let frame = self.frame().expect(...)` on every iteration. `crates/lyng-js/vm/src/frame.rs:126` defines `FrameRecord` as `Clone + Copy` with 19 fields (`code`, `instruction_offset`, `parameter_initializer_end_offset`, `registers`, `return_register`, `realm`, `lexical_env`, `variable_env`, `this_value`, `construct_this`, `new_target`, `callee`, `tail_caller`, `tail_caller_strict`, `handler_cursor`, `flags`, `kind`, `resume_kind`, `resume_value`, `resume_active`). Estimated size ~88 bytes; copied per opcode.

`installed.function.instructions()` is also re-fetched per iteration (three method calls + a Vec deref) even though it's stable until the frame is replaced.

lyng-3wvk reduced call-frame hot-path overhead at call entry but did not change per-opcode dispatch loop access. This issue is the per-opcode follow-up.

Goal: Refactor the inner dispatch loop so that immutable-per-activation state lives in locals (which LLVM can hoist into registers) and only the genuinely mutable bits (`instruction_offset`, `handler_cursor`, occasionally `lexical_env`, accumulator/resume state) are read/written.

Implementation sketch:
- Split `FrameRecord` semantically into "frame metadata" (stable per activation: `code`, `parameter_initializer_end_offset`, `registers.base`, `registers.len`, `return_register`, `realm`, `variable_env`, `this_value`, `construct_this`, `new_target`, `callee`, `tail_caller`, `tail_caller_strict`, `kind`) and "frame state" (mutable: `instruction_offset`, `handler_cursor`, `lexical_env`, `resume_kind`, `resume_value`, `resume_active`, `flags`).
- In the dispatch outer loop (after Epic 1.1's byte-stream conversion), pick up the frame once per activation and bind locals: `let mut pc: *const u8 = ...; let bytecode_base: *const u8 = ...; let bytecode_end: *const u8 = ...; let register_base: u32 = ...; let installed: &InstalledFunction = ...; let realm = ...; etc.` Only write back to `self.frames` on call, return, throw, or async suspend.
- Pass `&mut FrameState` (small mutable struct) to opcode helpers instead of `FrameRecord`. Reserve `FrameRecord` for cold helpers and debug inspection.
- Preserve rooting, unwinding, for-in/iterator cleanup, and mapped-arguments finalization invariants from lyng-3wvk.

Related prior work:
- lyng-3wvk (Reduce call-frame hot-path size, closed) — call-entry side, this builds on
- lyng-5zky (Eliminate register access bounds checks, closed) — preserves
- lyng-2hhp (Threaded dispatch prototype, closed) — this issue lives inside the new dispatch loop from Epic 3.1

Dependencies: lyng-2yow-1.1 (byte stream — `pc` as `*const u8` is natural). Conceptually independent of 1.2, 1.3, 1.4. Strongly synergistic with Epic 3.1 (the new dispatch loop is the place where the hoisting lives).
acceptance: Per-opcode runtime cost drops. Verified via `bench runtime --preset profile-target` on `array-heavy.iterator-runtime` or `class-heavy.runtime`. Profiler output (`sample` or `xctrace`) confirms `Vm::frame` / `FrameRecord` copying are no longer in the per-opcode hot path. Rooting and unwinding invariants from lyng-3wvk preserved. `cargo test -p lyng-js-vm` passes. Test262 conformance unchanged. `compare` arithmetic-loop and array-object-loop show measurable improvement over the 2026-05-12 baselines. The dcat handoff includes a flamegraph comparison and per-opcode cycle-count estimate.

notes:
Implemented dispatch-loop frame-state hoist work for the match dispatcher.

Changes:
- `run_match` now fetches the active frame code once in an outer activation loop, caches the `InstalledFunction` allocation for that code, and runs an inner opcode loop until the active top frame switches code.
- The inner dispatch path no longer calls `self.frame()` per opcode; it reads the active frame directly and uses a stable raw pointer to the Arc-owned `InstalledFunction` payload to avoid per-opcode Arc cloning.
- Added a test-only `FrameMetadata` / `FrameState` split plus `frame::tests::dispatch_state_writeback_updates_mutable_fields_only` to pin the intended stable-vs-mutable frame semantics.

description:
Replace the linear-scan polymorphic IC lookup with a hashed or branched data structure. Keep the 8-entry capacity set in lyng-1xig.

Current state: `crates/lyng-js/vm/src/vm/feedback.rs:15` sets `POLYMORPHIC_PROPERTY_CACHE_LIMIT = 8` (raised from 4 in lyng-1xig). The `NamedPropertyFeedback::entries: [Option<NamedPropertyCacheEntry>; 8]` array is scanned linearly via `active_entries()` on every IC lookup. lyng-1xig added receiver-shape prefiltering before full validation, which helps, but the underlying scan is still up to 8 comparisons.

V8's IC uses 4 inline entries with a hashed/sorted-by-shape access pattern; JSC's `StructureStubInfo` similarly. - Unroll the lookup to 8 explicit cmp+branch pairs and let LLVM optimize (already partially the case; verify the codegen).
- Maintain a small (4-element) LRU front cache atop the 8-entry pool — common cases hit the front cache in 1-2 compares.

Implementation sketch:
- Change the `entries` array storage strategy in `NamedPropertyFeedback` and `KeyedPropertyFeedback`.
- Update insert / lookup paths to preserve invalidation epoch tracking.

title: Improve polymorphic IC lookup data structure
Hoist frame state into dispatch-loop locals
description:
Hoist immutable-per-activation frame state into the dispatch loop's locals, removing per-opcode `FrameRecord` copies.

Current state: `crates/lyng-js/vm/src/vm/dispatch.rs:99` does `let frame = self.frame().expect(...)` on every iteration. `crates/lyng-js/vm/src/frame.rs:126` defines `FrameRecord` as `Clone + Copy` with 19 fields (`code`, `instruction_offset`, `parameter_initializer_end_offset`, `registers`, `return_register`, `realm`, `lexical_env`, `variable_env`, `this_value`, `construct_this`, `new_target`, `callee`, `tail_caller`, `tail_caller_strict`, `handler_cursor`, `flags`, `kind`, `resume_kind`, `resume_value`, `resume_active`). Estimated size ~88 bytes; copied per opcode.

`installed.function.instructions()` is also re-fetched per iteration (three method calls + a Vec deref) even though it's stable until the frame is replaced.

lyng-3wvk reduced call-frame hot-path overhead at call entry but did not change per-opcode dispatch loop access. This issue is the per-opcode follow-up.

Goal: Refactor the inner dispatch loop so that immutable-per-activation state lives in locals (which LLVM can hoist into registers) and only the genuinely mutable bits (`instruction_offset`, `handler_cursor`, occasionally `lexical_env`, accumulator/resume state) are read/written.

Implementation sketch:
- Split `FrameRecord` semantically into "frame metadata" (stable per activation: `code`, `parameter_initializer_end_offset`, `registers.base`, `registers.len`, `return_register`, `realm`, `variable_env`, `this_value`, `construct_this`, `new_target`, `callee`, `tail_caller`, `tail_caller_strict`, `kind`) and "frame state" (mutable: `instruction_offset`, `handler_cursor`, `lexical_env`, `resume_kind`, `resume_value`, `resume_active`, `flags`).
- In the dispatch outer loop (after Epic 1.1's byte-stream conversion), pick up the frame once per activation and bind locals: `let mut pc: *const u8 = ...; let bytecode_base: *const u8 = ...; let bytecode_end: *const u8 = ...; let register_base: u32 = ...; let installed: &InstalledFunction = ...; let realm = ...; etc.` Only write back to `self.frames` on call, return, throw, or async suspend.
- Pass `&mut FrameState` (small mutable struct) to opcode helpers instead of `FrameRecord`. Reserve `FrameRecord` for cold helpers and debug inspection.
- Preserve rooting, unwinding, for-in/iterator cleanup, and mapped-arguments finalization invariants from lyng-3wvk.

Related prior work:
- lyng-3wvk (Reduce call-frame hot-path size, closed) — call-entry side, this builds on
- lyng-5zky (Eliminate register access bounds checks, closed) — preserves
- lyng-2hhp (Threaded dispatch prototype, closed) — this issue lives inside the new dispatch loop from Epic 3.1

Dependencies: lyng-2yow-1.1 (byte stream — `pc` as `*const u8` is natural). Conceptually independent of 1.2, 1.3, 1.4. Strongly synergistic with Epic 3.1 (the new dispatch loop is the place where the hoisting lives).

Profiler output (`sample` or `xctrace`) confirms `Vm::frame` / `FrameRecord` copying are no longer in the per-opcode hot path. Rooting and unwinding invariants from lyng-3wvk preserved. `cargo test -p lyng-js-vm` passes. Test262 conformance unchanged. `compare` arithmetic-loop and array-object-loop show measurable improvement over the 2026-05-12 baselines. The dcat handoff includes a flamegraph comparison and per-opcode cycle-count estimate.

title: Hoist frame state into dispatch-loop locals
Convert bytecode storage to Vec<u8> byte stream
description:
Replace `Vec<Instruction>` bytecode storage with `Vec<u8>` byte-stream encoding.

Current state: `crates/lyng-js/bytecode/src/instruction.rs` defines `Instruction` as a Rust enum with three forms (`Abc`, `Abx`, `Ax`). The on-wire encoding via `Instruction::encode_word()` is 4 bytes, but the in-memory `size_of::<Instruction>()` is 8 bytes (discriminant + Ax-form i32 padding, confirmed by mock compile on aarch64-darwin stable Rust).

`crates/lyng-js/bytecode/src/function/template.rs:25` stores `instructions: Vec<Instruction>` on `BytecodeFunction`. `crates/lyng-js/vm/src/vm/dispatch.rs:98-129` per-iteration does `installed.function.instructions().get(i).copied()` — fetching 8 bytes from an arbitrary heap location, matching on the enum discriminant, then matching on the inner opcode.

QuickJS bytecode averages 1.5-2 bytes/op (variable-width byte stream with computed-goto dispatch). V8 Ignition averages similar via accumulator-based ISA with operand-scale prefixes. lyng-js pushes 3-5x more bytecode bytes through the I-cache for the same logical instruction stream.

Goal: Change the storage to `Vec<u8>` carrying the existing 4-byte `Instruction::encode_word()` payload. Keep the logical instruction set unchanged. Decoder reads opcode byte, then operand bytes by opcode-dictated width.

Implementation sketch:
- Replace `instructions: Vec<Instruction>` with `instructions: Vec<u8>` on `BytecodeFunction`.
- Add per-opcode operand-width tables in `lyng_js_bytecode::opcode` (every opcode fits one of the existing 3 forms, so the table is small and constant).
- Rewrite `BytecodeFunctionBuilder` to emit raw bytes; preserve patching APIs (`patch_ax`, `patch_bx`) by writing into known byte positions.
- Rewrite decoder helpers in `bytecode/src/decoder.rs` to advance a cursor by opcode-dictated width.
- Update `vm/src/vm/dispatch.rs` to match on `u8` opcode at the top level (LLVM synthesizes a real jump table for a dense u8 match). Read operand bytes from the byte stream with `unsafe` indexed reads after a one-time bounds check at function entry that proves the stream is well-formed.
- Update `Disassembler` (in `crates/lyng-js/bytecode/src/disassembler.rs`) to walk byte width instead of `Vec<Instruction>`.
- Update `compiler/src/script/emit.rs` and related emit paths to use the new builder.

Related prior work:
- lyng-5u2z (Evaluate compact bytecode encoding for interpreter density, open) — this issue is the implementation; lyng-5u2z's evaluation/design phase is folded into this one. Close lyng-5u2z when this lands.
- lyng-342b (Compact installed bytecode metadata side tables, closed) — orthogonal but adjacent; verify no regressions in metadata layout.
- lyng-26wf (Smi specialization opcodes, closed) — preserve all specialized opcodes added there.

Risk: high blast radius. Touches bytecode IR, compiler emitter, VM decoder, disassembler, and any tooling that reads bytecode. Land as one focused change with full Test262 + density verification, or behind a temporary `bytecode_v2` feature flag if the change is too large to land atomically.

title: Convert bytecode storage to Vec<u8> byte stream
Convert bytecode storage to Vec<u8> byte stream
description:
Replace `Vec<Instruction>` bytecode storage with `Vec<u8>` byte-stream encoding.

Current state: `crates/lyng-js/bytecode/src/instruction.rs` defines `Instruction` as a Rust enum with three forms (`Abc`, `Abx`, `Ax`). The on-wire encoding via `Instruction::encode_word()` is 4 bytes, but the in-memory `size_of::<Instruction>()` is 8 bytes (discriminant + Ax-form i32 padding, confirmed by mock compile on aarch64-darwin stable Rust).

`crates/lyng-js/bytecode/src/function/template.rs:25` stores `instructions: Vec<Instruction>` on `BytecodeFunction`. `crates/lyng-js/vm/src/vm/dispatch.rs:98-129` per-iteration does `installed.function.instructions().get(i).copied()` — fetching 8 bytes from an arbitrary heap location, matching on the enum discriminant, then matching on the inner opcode.

QuickJS bytecode averages 1.5-2 bytes/op (variable-width byte stream with computed-goto dispatch). V8 Ignition averages similar via accumulator-based ISA with operand-scale prefixes. lyng-js pushes 3-5x more bytecode bytes through the I-cache for the same logical instruction stream.

Goal: Change the storage to `Vec<u8>` carrying the existing 4-byte `Instruction::encode_word()` payload. Keep the logical instruction set unchanged. Decoder reads opcode byte, then operand bytes by opcode-dictated width.

Implementation sketch:
- Replace `instructions: Vec<Instruction>` with `instructions: Vec<u8>` on `BytecodeFunction`.
- Add per-opcode operand-width tables in `lyng_js_bytecode::opcode` (every opcode fits one of the existing 3 forms, so the table is small and constant).
- Rewrite `BytecodeFunctionBuilder` to emit raw bytes; preserve patching APIs (`patch_ax`, `patch_bx`) by writing into known byte positions.
- Rewrite decoder helpers in `bytecode/src/decoder.rs` to advance a cursor by opcode-dictated width.
- Update `vm/src/vm/dispatch.rs` to match on `u8` opcode at the top level (LLVM synthesizes a real jump table for a dense u8 match). Read operand bytes from the byte stream with `unsafe` indexed reads after a one-time bounds check at function entry that proves the stream is well-formed.
- Update `Disassembler` (in `crates/lyng-js/bytecode/src/disassembler.rs`) to walk byte width instead of `Vec<Instruction>`.
- Update `compiler/src/script/emit.rs` and related emit paths to use the new builder.

title: Hoist frame state into dispatch-loop locals
description:
Hoist immutable-per-activation frame state into the dispatch loop's locals, removing per-opcode `FrameRecord` copies.

Current state: `crates/lyng-js/vm/src/vm/dispatch.rs:99` does `let frame = self.frame().expect(...)` on every iteration. `crates/lyng-js/vm/src/frame.rs:126` defines `FrameRecord` as `Clone + Copy` with 19 fields (`code`, `instruction_offset`, `parameter_initializer_end_offset`, `registers`, `return_register`, `realm`, `lexical_env`, `variable_env`, `this_value`, `construct_this`, `new_target`, `callee`, `tail_caller`, `tail_caller_strict`, `handler_cursor`, `flags`, `kind`, `resume_kind`, `resume_value`, `resume_active`). Estimated size ~88 bytes; copied per opcode.

`installed.function.instructions()` is also re-fetched per iteration (three method calls + a Vec deref) even though it's stable until the frame is replaced.

lyng-3wvk reduced call-frame hot-path overhead at call entry but did not change per-opcode dispatch loop access. This issue is the per-opcode follow-up.

Goal: Refactor the inner dispatch loop so that immutable-per-activation state lives in locals (which LLVM can hoist into registers) and only the genuinely mutable bits (`instruction_offset`, `handler_cursor`, occasionally `lexical_env`, accumulator/resume state) are read/written.

Implementation sketch:
- Split `FrameRecord` semantically into "frame metadata" (stable per activation: `code`, `parameter_initializer_end_offset`, `registers.base`, `registers.len`, `return_register`, `realm`, `variable_env`, `this_value`, `construct_this`, `new_target`, `callee`, `tail_caller`, `tail_caller_strict`, `kind`) and "frame state" (mutable: `instruction_offset`, `handler_cursor`, `lexical_env`, `resume_kind`, `resume_value`, `resume_active`, `flags`).
- In the dispatch outer loop (after Epic 1.1's byte-stream conversion), pick up the frame once per activation and bind locals: `let mut pc: *const u8 = ...; let bytecode_base: *const u8 = ...; let bytecode_end: *const u8 = ...; let register_base: u32 = ...; let installed: &InstalledFunction = ...; let realm = ...; etc.` Only write back to `self.frames` on call, return, throw, or async suspend.
- Pass `&mut FrameState` (small mutable struct) to opcode helpers instead of `FrameRecord`. Reserve `FrameRecord` for cold helpers and debug inspection.
- Preserve rooting, unwinding, for-in/iterator cleanup, and mapped-arguments finalization invariants from lyng-3wvk.

Related prior work:
- lyng-3wvk (Reduce call-frame hot-path size, closed) — call-entry side, this builds on
- lyng-5zky (Eliminate register access bounds checks, closed) — preserves
- lyng-2hhp (Threaded dispatch prototype, closed) — this issue lives inside the new dispatch loop from Epic 3.1

Dependencies: lyng-2yow-1.1 (byte stream — `pc` as `*const u8` is natural). Conceptually independent of 1.2, 1.3, 1.4. Strongly synergistic with Epic 3.1 (the new dispatch loop is the place where the hoisting lives).
acceptance: Per-opcode runtime cost drops. Verified via `bench runtime --preset profile-target` on `array-heavy.iterator-runtime` or `class-heavy.runtime`. Profiler output (`sample` or `xctrace`) confirms `Vm::frame` / `FrameRecord` copying are no longer in the per-opcode hot path. Rooting and unwinding invariants from lyng-3wvk preserved. `cargo test -p lyng-js-vm` passes. Test262 conformance unchanged. `compare` arithmetic-loop and array-object-loop show measurable improvement over the 2026-05-12 baselines. The dcat handoff includes a flamegraph comparison and per-opcode cycle-count estimate.
notes:
Implemented dispatch-loop frame-state hoist work for the match dispatcher.

Changes:
- `run_match` now fetches the active frame code once in an outer activation loop, caches the `InstalledFunction` allocation for that code, and runs an inner opcode loop until the active top frame switches code.
- The inner dispatch path no longer calls `self.frame()` per opcode; it reads the active frame directly and uses a stable raw pointer to the Arc-owned `InstalledFunction` payload to avoid per-opcode Arc cloning.
- Added a test-only `FrameMetadata` / `FrameState` split plus `frame::tests::dispatch_state_writeback_updates_mutable_fields_only` to pin the intended stable-vs-mutable frame semantics.
- Preserved call, return, throw, async suspend, and frame replacement behavior by breaking back to the outer loop when the active frame code changes.

title: Improve polymorphic IC lookup data structure
description:
Replace the linear-scan polymorphic IC lookup with a hashed or branched data structure. Keep the 8-entry capacity set in lyng-1xig.

Current state: `crates/lyng-js/vm/src/vm/feedback.rs:15` sets `POLYMORPHIC_PROPERTY_CACHE_LIMIT = 8` (raised from 4 in lyng-1xig). The `NamedPropertyFeedback::entries: [Option<NamedPropertyCacheEntry>; 8]` array is scanned linearly via `active_entries()` on every IC lookup. lyng-1xig added receiver-shape prefiltering before full validation, which helps, but the underlying scan is still up to 8 comparisons.

V8's IC uses 4 inline entries with a hashed/sorted-by-shape access pattern; JSC's `StructureStubInfo` similarly. The 8-entry capacity was set to preserve feedback for 4-8 shape sites; lyng-1xig found no measured perf change vs. the previous 4-entry limit (both showed 1.91x QuickJS on polymorphic-property-loop), suggesting the linear scan itself is the limiting factor.

Goal: Improve the polymorphic IC lookup data structure so the per-access cost scales sub-linearly with entry count. Keep the 8-entry capacity. Preserve receiver-shape prefiltering, stale-shape rejection, and invalidation correctness.

Options to evaluate (pick one or compare with measurement):
- Sort entries by `receiver_shape` and do a binary search.
- Hash entries by `receiver_shape & mask` into a 2-way or 4-way set-associative inline cache; fall back to linear scan within a set.
- Unroll the lookup to 8 explicit cmp+branch pairs and let LLVM optimize (already partially the case; verify the codegen).
- Maintain a small (4-element) LRU front cache atop the 8-entry pool — common cases hit the front cache in 1-2 compares.

Implementation sketch:
- Change the `entries` array storage strategy in `NamedPropertyFeedback` and `KeyedPropertyFeedback`.
- Update insert / lookup paths to preserve invalidation epoch tracking.
- Verify cache-state transitions (Uninitialized -> Monomorphic -> Polymorphic -> Megamorphic) work the same; add tests for transitions.
- Re-run the polymorphic-property-loop benchmark added in lyng-1xig.

Related prior work:
- lyng-1xig (Relax IC cliff, closed) — preserve capacity (8); change is the lookup data structure, not the capacity
- lyng-46rj (Adaptive dict, closed) — orthogonal

Dependencies: cleaner to land after 1.3 because both touch `feedback.rs`. Independent of 1.1 / 1.2 / 1.5.
acceptance: `diagnostics.megamorphic_sites` in the bench JSON does not increase. `diagnostics.live_feedback_sites` unchanged. `cargo run --release -p lyng-js-bench -- compare --filter polymorphic-property-loop` shows non-regression vs. the lyng-1xig baseline of 1.91x QuickJS, with measurable improvement once the cache has 5+ shapes. Cache state transitions tested via `cargo test -p lyng-js-vm`. Test262 conformance unchanged. The dcat handoff records before/after per-shape-count median times.
notes:
Implemented sorted polymorphic named-property IC lookup.

Changes:
- `NamedPropertyFeedback` keeps the active 8-entry prefix sorted by `receiver_shape` and uses `binary_search_by` for load/store lookup and replacement.
- `KeyedPropertyFeedback` keeps named-atom entries sorted by `(atom, receiver_shape)` and uses binary search for keyed named load/store lookup and replacement.
- The 8-entry polymorphic capacity is unchanged.
- Existing stale-shape and invalidation behavior is preserved by still validating through `load_from_named_property_cache` / `store_to_named_property_cache` after the shape lookup hits.
- Added red/green tests:
  - `named_property_load_ic_orders_polymorphic_entries_by_shape`
  - `keyed_named_atom_ic_orders_polymorphic_entries_by_shape`
  These initially failed with descending insertion order, then passed after the sorted-prefix implementation. Existing polymorphic and megamorphic transition tests still pass.

Verification:
- `cargo test -p lyng-js-vm inline_caches`: 20 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo test -p lyng-js-vm`: 355 passed, 0 failed; doctests 0 passed.
- `cargo fmt --all --check`: passed.
- `cargo clippy -p lyng-js-vm --all-targets -- -W clippy::pedantic -W clippy::nursery`: passed with no warnings.
- `cargo run --release -p lyng-js-test262 -- --report /tmp/lyng-js-test262-54ji.md -j 12`: 49,724 passed files, 5 failed files, 0 panics, 3,324 skips. This matches the previous whole-corpus conformance shape.

- `cargo run --release -p lyng-js-bench -- compare --filter polymorphic-property-loop --samples 9 --warmup-samples 2 --report /tmp/lyng-js-compare-54ji-polymorphic-property-loop.md --json /tmp/lyng-js-compare-54ji-polymorphic-property-loop.json`

description:

Current state: `crates/lyng-js/vm/src/vm/feedback.rs:15` sets `POLYMORPHIC_PROPERTY_CACHE_LIMIT = 8` (raised from 4 in lyng-1xig). The `NamedPropertyFeedback::entries: [Option<NamedPropertyCacheEntry>; 8]` array is scanned linearly via `active_entries()` on every IC lookup. lyng-1xig added receiver-shape prefiltering before full validation, which helps, but the underlying scan is still up to 8 comparisons.

V8's IC uses 4 inline entries with a hashed/sorted-by-shape access pattern; JSC's `StructureStubInfo` similarly. The 8-entry capacity was set to preserve feedback for 4-8 shape sites; lyng-1xig found no measured perf change vs. the previous 4-entry limit (both showed 1.91x QuickJS on polymorphic-property-loop), suggesting the linear scan itself is the limiting factor.

Goal: Improve the polymorphic IC lookup data structure so the per-access cost scales sub-linearly with entry count. Keep the 8-entry capacity. Preserve receiver-shape prefiltering, stale-shape rejection, and invalidation correctness.

- Hash entries by `receiver_shape & mask` into a 2-way or 4-way set-associative inline cache; fall back to linear scan within a set.
- Unroll the lookup to 8 explicit cmp+branch pairs and let LLVM optimize (already partially the case; verify the codegen).
- Maintain a small (4-element) LRU front cache atop the 8-entry pool — common cases hit the front cache in 1-2 compares.

- Change the `entries` array storage strategy in `NamedPropertyFeedback` and `KeyedPropertyFeedback`.
