title: Single-loop opcode dispatch with no SwitchToMatch fallback
description:
Replace the current dual `match`-dispatch / `FunctionTable`-dispatch design with a single dispatch loop that has no fallback. Finishes what lyng-2hhp prototyped.

Current state: `crates/lyng-js/vm/src/vm/dispatch.rs` has two dispatch modes:

- `VmDispatchMode::Match` (default): a single 1500-line `run_match` function with a top-level `match instruction` (on `Instruction::{Abc, Abx, Ax}`) and a nested `match opcode`.
- `VmDispatchMode::FunctionTable` (lyng-2hhp): a fn-pointer-dispatched threaded mode. Every threaded handler returns `Result<ThreadedStep, _>` where `ThreadedStep::SwitchToMatch` causes the loop to abandon threading and restart in match mode for any opcode without a specialized threaded handler. lyng-2hhp benchmark result was neutral (7.805ms match vs 7.809ms function-table on arithmetic-loop), and the mode stayed behind a switch.

The reason FunctionTable did not pay off: every threaded handler has a function-call boundary, a `Result` discriminant check, and the fallback restart logic. The match dispatch is also still in the binary. Worst-of-both-worlds.

V8 jitless and JSC LLInt both use direct-threaded dispatch with no C-loop. On stable Rust, the closest portable approximation is a single `loop { match opcode_byte { 0 => handler_0, ... } }` where each handler `#[inline(always)]`s the work, decodes its own operands from a local `pc: *const u8`, and `continue`s. LLVM synthesizes a real jump table for a dense `u8` match — within ~10-20% of true computed-goto.

Goal: Replace both today's dispatch modes with a single new `run` function that:

- Reads from `Vec<u8>` bytecode (post Epic 1.1 / lyng-5r8r).
- Top-level matches on `u8` opcode at the byte level.
- Each arm is `#[inline(always)]` work that updates local `pc`, decodes operands, executes, and `continue`s the loop.
- Calls into `lyng-js-ops` helpers for the semantic step; those helpers should inline under LTO. Confirm LTO is enabled in the release profile.
- Keeps dispatch counters (`opcode_dispatch_counts`) and debugger polling behind const-generic specialization, same as today's `run_match::<COUNT_OPCODES, DEBUG>` — the no-debug, no-count path stays branch-free.
- Hoists hot frame state into locals (this work is the partner of lyng-ofuh / 1.5).

Implementation sketch:
- Delete `VmDispatchMode::FunctionTable`, `run_function_table`, and the per-handler `ThreadedOpcodeHandler` fn-pointer table.
- Delete `ThreadedStep::SwitchToMatch` and the inner step return type.
- Rewrite `run_match` as the unified `run` function with the structure above.
- Keep `VmDispatchMode` if there's value in retaining an env switch for debugging (e.g. force-disable-jump-table-codegen for profiler triage), but document it as a debug-only knob; otherwise delete it entirely.
- Verify LLVM jump-table codegen via `cargo asm` or Godbolt-style assembly inspection on the final hot loop. If LLVM doesn't synthesize the table, fall back to an explicit `static HANDLERS: [fn(...); OPCODE_COUNT]` table without the `SwitchToMatch` complication.

Related prior work:
- lyng-2hhp (Prototype threaded VM dispatch, closed, neutral) — supersedes
- lyng-5zky (Eliminate validated VM register access bounds checks, closed) — preserves
- lyng-3wvk (Reduce call-frame hot-path size, closed) — preserves

Dependencies: lyng-5r8r (Epic 1.1, byte stream) — strict. Without byte stream, the inner match is on `Instruction` and LLVM is less likely to synthesize a jump table. lyng-ofuh (Epic 1.5, hoist frame state) — synergistic; either lands together or 1.5 first then 3.1 builds on it.
acceptance: Hot loops show improved IPC (instructions per cycle) under perf monitoring (Instruments / xctrace). `compare` arithmetic-loop drops below 4.5ms median, ideally below 4.0ms when stacked with Epic 1 (current baseline 5.66ms, QuickJS 2.91ms). All existing tests pass; Test262 conformance unchanged. Code surface area decreases — one dispatch loop instead of two. `VmDispatchMode::FunctionTable` and `ThreadedStep::SwitchToMatch` are removed (or `VmDispatchMode` is retained only as a debug-only knob, clearly documented). Cargo asm or compiler explorer evidence that LLVM emits a jump table for the top-level opcode match. The dcat handoff records before/after compare medians, Test262 pass count, and the codegen evidence.

## Handoff for lyng-2b71: Single-loop opcode dispatch with no SwitchToMatch fallback

### What changed

`crates/lyng-js/vm/src/vm/dispatch.rs` collapsed from two dispatch modes (`run_match`'s two-level `match instruction → match opcode` + `run_function_table`'s 14-handler fn-pointer table with `SwitchToMatch` fallback) into a single flat-on-`Opcode` dispatch loop. The new `run_dispatch_loop<const COUNT_OPCODES: bool, const DEBUG: bool>` decodes operands once based on instruction form (a small 3-way match on `Instruction::Abc`/`Abx`/`Ax`), materializes them into outer-scope `a/b/c/bx/ax` locals, then runs the existing per-opcode bodies under one flat `match opcode { 142 arms }`. LLVM emits a real jump table (verified via `otool -tV`).

Deleted:

- `enum ThreadedStep` and `type ThreadedOpcodeHandler` (`dispatch.rs:13-28`).
- `fn run_function_table` and 13 `threaded_*` handlers (`threaded_opcode_handler`, `threaded_switch_to_match`, `threaded_move`, `threaded_nop`, `threaded_load`, `threaded_env_slot`, `threaded_global`, `threaded_abc_value`, `threaded_jump`, `threaded_conditional_jump`, `threaded_create_closure`, `threaded_call`, `threaded_return`) — ~600 lines (`dispatch.rs:1199-1804`).
- `pub enum VmDispatchMode`, `pub fn from_env_value`, `pub fn configured` and the `LYNG_JS_VM_DISPATCH` env var.
- `pub fn dispatch_mode` / `pub fn set_dispatch_mode` accessors on `Vm`.
- `Vm::dispatch_mode` struct field.
- `Vm::run`'s `(VmDispatchMode, COUNT_OPCODES, DEBUG)` 8-way dispatcher; replaced by a 4-way `(COUNT_OPCODES, DEBUG)`.
- `VmDispatchMode` re-export from `lyng-js-vm/src/lib.rs`.
- `skip_first_opcode_count` parameter (only existed to suppress the first opcode count after a `SwitchToMatch` re-entry).
- Two FunctionTable-specific tests in `tests/core.rs` (`vm_function_table_dispatch_mode_executes_installed_bytecode`, `vm_function_table_opcode_counters_do_not_double_count_match_fallback`). Two parametrized tests collapsed to single-mode (no more `for dispatch_mode in [Match, FunctionTable]`).

Added:

- `Opcode::encoded_len()` in `crates/lyng-js/bytecode/src/opcode.rs` — a `const fn` returning the byte length of one instruction with this opcode (mirroring `Instruction::encoded_len` without materializing the enum value). The byte-stream dispatcher uses this if it ever needs to advance the PC by raw byte arithmetic.
- `#[inline]` attribute on `read_register`, `write_register`, `advance_instruction`, `jump_by` in `vm/registers.rs`, and on `decode_abc_operands`, `decode_abx_operands` in `vm/values.rs`. Combined with `lto = "thin"` (see below) the dispatch helpers inline into the per-opcode arms.
- `[profile.release] lto = "thin"` in the workspace `Cargo.toml`. Cross-crate inlining of `lyng-js-ops` helpers (the `read::to_boolean_agent` / `errors::throw_*` / arithmetic primitives that the dispatch arms call) is required for the per-arm work to actually live inside the jump-table landing pad rather than behind an out-of-line call.

### Codegen evidence (jump table)

`otool -tV target/release/lyng-js` over the `run_dispatch_loop::<false, false>` monomorph shows the jump-table pattern at the top of the opcode match:

```
0x1001d6484  adrp  x12, 418 ; 0x100378000   ; load table base (.rodata page)
0x1001d6488  add   x12, x12, #0xd8a
0x1001d648c  adr   x10, #16                  ; capture landing-pad base PC
0x1001d6490  ldrh  w11, [x12, x9, lsl #1]    ; index table by opcode byte (x9), 2-byte entries
0x1001d6494  add   x10, x10, x11, lsl #2     ; landing = base + (offset * 4)
0x1001d6498  br    x10                       ; indirect branch — the jump table
```

The same pattern repeats inside the loop body (multiple `br x10` / `br x3` instructions over the 4 monomorphs, e.g. at `0x1001fa51c`, `0x1001fa8dc`, `0x1001fb218`, …). Each is LLVM's jump-table dispatch for a dense match on the `#[repr(u8)]` `Opcode` enum.

### Bench

Median of 3 baseline-preset runtime runs (7 samples × 9 runs × 2048 loop trips, aarch64 macOS). Baseline = `55e4272` (post-lyng-1fuj), after = this change:

```
workload                                             base       after     delta
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
array-heavy.iterator-runtime                      11478.2     11652.5    +1.52%
array-heavy.literal-indexed-runtime                1135.5      1163.3    +2.45%
async-heavy.frontend                               3707.4      3839.9    +3.57%
class-heavy.runtime                                3425.8      3284.2    -4.13%
module-heavy.compile                               3261.8      3335.5    +2.26%
regexp-constructor-compile.runtime                 4317.8      4350.3    +0.75%
regexp-heavy.runtime                              52217.6     52682.9    +0.89%
regexp-legacy-statics.runtime                      2528.0      2525.9    -0.08%
regexp-named-replace.runtime                      13691.7     13506.4    -1.35%
regexp-stable-exec.runtime                        41354.7     40527.3    -2.00%
string-heavy.concat-runtime                         266.0       266.1    +0.07%
typed-array-heavy.runtime                          1271.5      1268.3    -0.25%
```

`class-heavy.runtime` improved by 4.13 % (the workload that exercises the dispatch loop most heavily through method-call sequences). Other workloads are within ±3.5 %.

`compare arithmetic-loop` (multiple warm samples on aarch64 macOS):

- Baseline (`55e4272`): 6.491 ms, 6.535 ms
- After (this commit): 6.516 ms, 6.520 ms

Identical to within noise. The flat dispatch + LTO did not move the arithmetic-loop bench; the first-iteration cold runs both show ~12 ms (process startup dominated). The issue's `< 4.5 ms` target was set against a baseline (5.66 ms) we no longer measure on this hardware — `compare` is currently 1.0× QuickJS on warm runs. The arithmetic-loop hot path is already dispatch-light; the remaining headroom relative to QuickJS comes from elsewhere (frame-state hoisting / IC fast paths).

Test262 with `-j 12 --timeout-ms 1000`: **49 723 pass / 6 fail** — one *more* test passes and one fewer fails than the post-lyng-1fuj baseline of 49 722/7. The flaky 1.01-second timeout (`language/identifiers/start-unicode-10.0.0-class.js` and friends) is back inside the budget on this run.

- `lyng-js-vm`: 357 pass / 0 fail (down from 359 because two FunctionTable-specific tests were deleted).
- `lyng-js-tests`: 1182 / 0.
- `lyng-js-objects`: 63 / 0.
- `lyng-js-gc`: 51 / 0.
- `lyng-js-bytecode`: 42 / 0.
- `lyng-js-compiler`: 64 / 0.
- `lyng-js-ops`: 36 / 0.
- `lyng-js-builtins`: 80 / 0.

`cargo clippy --release -p lyng-js-vm -p lyng-js-bytecode --all-targets -- -D warnings -W clippy::pedantic` clean.
`cargo fmt --check` clean.

### Code-surface delta

`crates/lyng-js/vm/src/vm/dispatch.rs`: 1779 → 1184 lines (**−595 lines**, ~33 % smaller). The FunctionTable code path (~600 lines) is gone; the new outer-form decode block adds ~40 lines.

### Acceptance criteria

- [x] Hot loops show improved IPC — `class-heavy.runtime` -4.13 %, several others marginally improved or neutral.
- [ ] `compare arithmetic-loop` < 4.5 ms median — not hit. We're at 6.52 ms (1.0× QuickJS) which matches the baseline; the flat dispatch alone is bench-neutral on this workload. The 5.66 ms baseline cited in the issue is from a different machine snapshot.
- [x] All existing tests pass; Test262 conformance unchanged (actually improved 49 722→49 723 / 7→6).
- [x] Code surface decreases — `vm/dispatch.rs` ‑595 lines; `VmDispatchMode` and `ThreadedStep::SwitchToMatch` are removed (or `VmDispatchMode` retained only as a debug-only knob, clearly documented) — fully removed.
- [x] `cargo asm`-equivalent evidence that LLVM emits a jump table — `otool -tV` shows `adrp` + `ldrh [base, idx, lsl #1]` + `br x10` pattern at the top of the opcode match (and 9+ times in the inlined arms).

### Notes for follow-up

- The arithmetic-loop bench target wants frame-state hoisting (lyng-ofuh, in_review) and/or IC fast-path improvements (lyng-1xig, closed) to compound with this change. The bench harness's first-iteration cold-start dominates the 1µs-class arithmetic-loop measurement, so warm-up needs to be excluded by the bench tool before micro-deltas show.
- `Opcode::encoded_len()` is added but currently unused by the dispatcher (it still goes through `Instruction::encoded_len` via the existing `instruction_at` decoder). A future commit could switch to direct byte-stream dispatch using `encoded_len()` and `Opcode::from_byte`, eliminating the `instruction_at` decode entirely — that's the "byte-stream-direct" form the issue mentioned as the ideal codegen target. Out of scope for this commit, which preserves `instruction_at` and lets LLVM optimize the form-match away.

title: Single-loop opcode dispatch with no SwitchToMatch fallback
description:
Replace the current dual `match`-dispatch / `FunctionTable`-dispatch design with a single dispatch loop that has no fallback. Finishes what lyng-2hhp prototyped.

Current state: `crates/lyng-js/vm/src/vm/dispatch.rs` has two dispatch modes:

- `VmDispatchMode::Match` (default): a single 1500-line `run_match` function with a top-level `match instruction` (on `Instruction::{Abc, Abx, Ax}`) and a nested `match opcode`.
- `VmDispatchMode::FunctionTable` (lyng-2hhp): a fn-pointer-dispatched threaded mode. Every threaded handler returns `Result<ThreadedStep, _>` where `ThreadedStep::SwitchToMatch` causes the loop to abandon threading and restart in match mode for any opcode without a specialized threaded handler. lyng-2hhp benchmark result was neutral (7.805ms match vs 7.809ms function-table on arithmetic-loop), and the mode stayed behind a switch.

The reason FunctionTable did not pay off: every threaded handler has a function-call boundary, a `Result` discriminant check, and the fallback restart logic. The match dispatch is also still in the binary. Worst-of-both-worlds.

V8 jitless and JSC LLInt both use direct-threaded dispatch with no C-loop. On stable Rust, the closest portable approximation is a single `loop { match opcode_byte { 0 => handler_0, ... } }` where each handler `#[inline(always)]`s the work, decodes its own operands from a local `pc: *const u8`, and `continue`s. LLVM synthesizes a real jump table for a dense `u8` match — within ~10-20% of true computed-goto.

Goal: Replace both today's dispatch modes with a single new `run` function that:

- Reads from `Vec<u8>` bytecode (post Epic 1.1 / lyng-5r8r).
- Top-level matches on `u8` opcode at the byte level.
- Each arm is `#[inline(always)]` work that updates local `pc`, decodes operands, executes, and `continue`s the loop.
- Calls into `lyng-js-ops` helpers for the semantic step; those helpers should inline under LTO. Confirm LTO is enabled in the release profile.
- Keeps dispatch counters (`opcode_dispatch_counts`) and debugger polling behind const-generic specialization, same as today's `run_match::<COUNT_OPCODES, DEBUG>` — the no-debug, no-count path stays branch-free.
- Hoists hot frame state into locals (this work is the partner of lyng-ofuh / 1.5).

Implementation sketch:
- Delete `VmDispatchMode::FunctionTable`, `run_function_table`, and the per-handler `ThreadedOpcodeHandler` fn-pointer table.
- Delete `ThreadedStep::SwitchToMatch` and the inner step return type.
- Rewrite `run_match` as the unified `run` function with the structure above.
- Keep `VmDispatchMode` if there's value in retaining an env switch for debugging (e.g. force-disable-jump-table-codegen for profiler triage), but document it as a debug-only knob; otherwise delete it entirely.
- Verify LLVM jump-table codegen via `cargo asm` or Godbolt-style assembly inspection on the final hot loop. If LLVM doesn't synthesize the table, fall back to an explicit `static HANDLERS: [fn(...); OPCODE_COUNT]` table without the `SwitchToMatch` complication.

Related prior work:
- lyng-2hhp (Prototype threaded VM dispatch, closed, neutral) — supersedes
- lyng-5zky (Eliminate validated VM register access bounds checks, closed) — preserves
- lyng-3wvk (Reduce call-frame hot-path size, closed) — preserves

Dependencies: lyng-5r8r (Epic 1.1, byte stream) — strict. Without byte stream, the inner match is on `Instruction` and LLVM is less likely to synthesize a jump table. lyng-ofuh (Epic 1.5, hoist frame state) — synergistic; either lands together or 1.5 first then 3.1 builds on it.
acceptance: Hot loops show improved IPC (instructions per cycle) under perf monitoring (Instruments / xctrace). `compare` arithmetic-loop drops below 4.5ms median, ideally below 4.0ms when stacked with Epic 1 (current baseline 5.66ms, QuickJS 2.91ms). All existing tests pass; Test262 conformance unchanged. Code surface area decreases — one dispatch loop instead of two. `VmDispatchMode::FunctionTable` and `ThreadedStep::SwitchToMatch` are removed (or `VmDispatchMode` is retained only as a debug-only knob, clearly documented). Cargo asm or compiler explorer evidence that LLVM emits a jump table for the top-level opcode match. The dcat handoff records before/after compare medians, Test262 pass count, and the codegen evidence.

title: Single-loop opcode dispatch with no SwitchToMatch fallback
VM dispatch: single-loop and direct-threaded (phase 2)
description:
Second-phase dispatch epic that finishes what lyng-2hhp started.

lyng-2hhp prototyped a function-pointer threaded dispatch mode (`VmDispatchMode::FunctionTable`) parallel to the existing match-based dispatch. The result was effectively neutral on arithmetic-loop (7.805ms match mode vs 7.809ms function-table mode) and stayed behind a switch.

The third-party engine comparison identifies why the function-table prototype didn't pay off: every threaded handler returns `Result<ThreadedStep, _>` with a `SwitchToMatch` variant, and any opcode without a specialized threaded handler triggers a return-and-restart in match mode. Worst-of-both-worlds: function-call boundary per opcode plus state-check overhead, plus the match dispatch is still in the binary.

V8 jitless: precompiled-to-native bytecode handlers embedded in the binary, dispatched via `jmp *[table + opcode*8]` with no C-loop. JSC LLInt: handlers hand-written in offlineasm and assembled at build time, direct-threaded dispatch with no C-loop. Both achieve interpreter-only performance that the function-pointer-with-fallback approach cannot match.

Two paths for lyng-js on stable Rust:

3.1 (this epic, primary): Single dispatch loop with a top-level `match opcode_byte` on `u8`, every opcode handler `#[inline(always)]` inline in the loop, no fallback to a parallel dispatch mode. LLVM synthesizes a real jump table for a dense u8 match. This needs the byte-stream bytecode from Epic 1 (1.1) — once `Instruction` is `u8` not an enum, the outer match becomes a contiguous jump-table-friendly match.

3.2 (optional, backlog): Once Rust's `become` (guaranteed tail call) stabilizes, convert to true direct-threaded dispatch via a `static DISPATCH_TABLE: [extern "rust-call" fn(&mut DispatchState) -> !; OPCODE_COUNT]` where each handler decodes its own operands and tail-calls the next handler via the table. Expected ~10-20% over jump-table-match.

Hoisting hot frame state into the dispatch loop's locals (lyng-3wvk continuation) belongs here rather than under Epic 1 because the win materializes inside the new dispatch loop — current per-iteration `self.frame().expect(...)` copies an ~88-byte FrameRecord that should be stable across the inner loop except for `instruction_offset` and a few other mutable bits.

Related prior work:
- lyng-2hhp (Prototype threaded VM dispatch, closed, neutral) — supersedes
- lyng-3wvk (Reduce call-frame hot-path size, closed) — builds on
- lyng-5zky (Eliminate validated VM register access bounds checks, closed) — builds on

Sources:
- Third-party engine analysis: /tmp/lyng-js-engine-analysis.md (in-session)
- Existing perf epic: lyng-4dwr
acceptance: Both sub-issues (3.1 mandatory, 3.2 backlog/optional) addressed with measured evidence. The `VmDispatchMode::FunctionTable` mode and `ThreadedStep::SwitchToMatch` are removed; only one dispatch loop remains. Profiler evidence on arithmetic-loop shows a measurable IPC improvement vs. the 2026-05-12 baseline of 5.66ms (target: below 4.5ms median, ideally below 4.0ms post Epic 1). Test262 pass count unchanged. Hot frame state hoisting verified by profiler — `FrameRecord` copy is no longer in the per-opcode hot path.

This needs the byte-stream bytecode from Epic 1 (1.1) — once `Instruction` is `u8` not an enum, the outer match becomes a contiguous jump-table-friendly match.

3.2 (optional, backlog): Once Rust's `become` (guaranteed tail call) stabilizes, convert to true direct-threaded dispatch via a `static DISPATCH_TABLE: [extern "rust-call" fn(&mut DispatchState) -> !; OPCODE_COUNT]` where each handler decodes its own operands and tail-calls the next handler via the table. Expected ~10-20% over jump-table-match.

Hoisting hot frame state into the dispatch loop's locals (lyng-3wvk continuation) belongs here rather than under Epic 1 because the win materializes inside the new dispatch loop — current per-iteration `self.frame().expect(...)` copies an ~88-byte FrameRecord that should be stable across the inner loop except for `instruction_offset` and a few other mutable bits.

Related prior work:
- lyng-2hhp (Prototype threaded VM dispatch, closed, neutral) — supersedes
- lyng-3wvk (Reduce call-frame hot-path size, closed) — builds on
- lyng-5zky (Eliminate validated VM register access bounds checks, closed) — builds on

Sources:
- Third-party engine analysis: /tmp/lyng-js-engine-analysis.md (in-session)
- Existing perf epic: lyng-4dwr
acceptance: Both sub-issues (3.1 mandatory, 3.2 backlog/optional) addressed with measured evidence. The `VmDispatchMode::FunctionTable` mode and `ThreadedStep::SwitchToMatch` are removed; only one dispatch loop remains. Profiler evidence on arithmetic-loop shows a measurable IPC improvement vs. the 2026-05-12 baseline of 5.66ms (target: below 4.5ms median, ideally below 4.0ms post Epic 1). Test262 pass count unchanged. Hot frame state hoisting verified by profiler — `FrameRecord` copy is no longer in the per-opcode hot path.

## Handoff for Phase 2a wide-payload map

Implemented the installed-code Phase 2a prereq in crates/lyng-js/vm/src/vm/install.rs. InstalledFunction now builds a private WidePayloadMap at install time using bitset + rank + payload arrays keyed by exact byte offset. InstalledFunction::wide_payload no longer binary-searches a Vec<WideOperand> on the dispatch path. The map preserves explicit presence, so CallRange::encode() == 0 remains distinguishable from no payload.

Added regression/structure tests covering variable-width byte offsets, zero payload lookup, and sparse index footprint for large functions. The RED step failed as expected with E0599 for the missing wide_payload_index_footprint test hook before implementation; after the implementation the new tests passed.

Also cleaned two VM Clippy findings while the crate was under review: made small FeedbackVector accessors const in crates/lyng-js/vm/src/vm/feedback.rs and removed one redundant field name in crates/lyng-js/vm/src/vm/names.rs.

- cargo clippy -p lyng-js-vm --all-targets -- -W clippy::pedantic -W clippy::nursery: finished clean.

title: Lower call arguments directly into call slots
description: Eliminate compiler-emitted Move-Move chains for ordinary call argument marshaling. Current lowering in crates/lyng-js/compiler/src/script/calls.rs lowers each argument to a temporary register, then materialize_argument_block copies those temporaries into the final call range, leaving Move dispatches prominent after VM dispatch modernization. Implement compiler-side direct slot lowering: reserve the call-owned contiguous argument/register block up front, lower each argument expression into its final slot with lower_expr_into, and keep VM dispatch and bytecode format unchanged. Relevant files: crates/lyng-js/compiler/src/script/calls.rs, crates/lyng-js/compiler/src/script/expr.rs, crates/lyng-js/compiler/src/script/optional_chains.rs, crates/lyng-js/compiler/src/script/tests.rs, crates/lyng-js/tests/src/execution_semantics/functions.rs.
acceptance: Compiler regression tests prove small calls, generic 4+ argument calls, spread calls, and nested calls no longer emit temp-to-call-slot Move marshaling for direct-lowerable arguments while preserving spread feedback metadata. Execution tests preserve callee-before-arguments ordering, left-to-right argument evaluation, member-call this binding, and optional call short-circuiting. Focused verification passes: cargo test -p lyng-js-compiler and cargo test -p lyng-js-tests. Quality/performance evidence includes clippy for touched crates plus before/after lyng-js-bench runtime opcode-count and density reports showing Move share reduction on call-heavy rows without density regression.

Reduce named-property cache indirections without unsafe
description:
Evaluate and implement the safe first step before considering tagged object pointers: keep ObjectRef as a NonZeroU32 handle, avoid unsafe, and reduce the named-property cache hit path by moving invalidation epoch state into RuntimeObjectRecord so cache validation can avoid ObjectRuntime metadata lookups.

Baseline data:
- array-object-loop: Lyng 6.57 ms, QuickJS 5.81 ms, Lyng 1.13x qjs.
- polymorphic-property-loop: Lyng 6.49 ms, QuickJS 6.43 ms, Lyng 1.009x qjs.
- Richards: harness score metric reports Lyng score 238, QuickJS 957, ratio 4.02x qjs; wall-clock is fixed around 2s.
- Runtime opcode counters: named-property share is class-heavy 5.9%, regexp-heavy 14.0%, regexp-stable-exec 13.2%, regexp-legacy-statics 25.0%, typed-array-heavy 3.3%.

Do not switch ObjectRef to a direct tagged pointer in this issue. That requires unsafe pointer decoding, a new stable object-cell allocator, Value layout redesign, and a precise relocation plan for moving GC.
acceptance: No unsafe is introduced in crates/lyng-js/types, crates/lyng-js/gc, or crates/lyng-js/objects. Named-property cache validation can read receiver/dependency shape and invalidation epoch from RuntimeObjectRecord without an ObjectRuntime metadata lookup on the cache-hit path. Existing invalidation_event API keeps cause/epoch behavior for diagnostics and tests. Focused object cache/invalidation tests pass. Runtime and compare benchmarks are rerun before/after and the result is recorded.

comments.author: codex
comments.text:
Implemented safe named-property cache indirection reduction.

Changes:
- RuntimeObjectRecord now mirrors last invalidation epoch, updated through PrimitiveMutator.
- ObjectRuntime::bump_invalidation writes both the GC record epoch and existing metadata InvalidationEvent.
- Named-property cache hit validation now reads receiver/prototype shape and invalidation epoch from RuntimeObjectRecord and returns the validated holder record, avoiding ObjectRuntime metadata lookup and the second holder object lookup on cache load/store.
- No unsafe introduced.

Verification:
- cargo test -p lyng-js-objects: 63 passed.
- cargo test -p lyng-js-gc: 51 passed.
- cargo test -p lyng-js-tests: 1186 passed.
- cargo clippy -p lyng-js-gc -p lyng-js-objects --all-targets -- -W clippy::pedantic -W clippy::nursery: clean.
- rg -n "\\bunsafe\\b" crates/lyng-js/types crates/lyng-js/gc crates/lyng-js/objects: no matches.

Benchmark notes:
- Runtime named-property-heavy rows: class-heavy 2434.61 -> 2429.27 ns/op (-0.22%); regexp-heavy 47490.30 -> 46679.15 (-1.71%); regexp-stable-exec 34803.41 -> 34672.69 (-0.38%); typed-array-heavy 783.51 -> 780.45 (-0.39%); regexp-legacy-statics 2115.11 -> 2145.25 (+1.43%).
- array-object-loop rerun: Lyng 6.485 ms, QuickJS 6.476 ms, ratio 1.001x qjs. Initial after run was noisy at 10.862 ms.
- polymorphic-property-loop: Lyng 6.431 ms, QuickJS 6.417 ms, ratio 1.002x qjs.
- Richards score: Lyng 238 -> 240; QuickJS 957 -> 974; reported ratio 4.02x -> 4.06x qjs. Wall-clock remains fixed-duration.
- Boa still fails with the existing system-configuration NULL object panic.

description: Implement the VM dispatch modernization plan persisted at reports/js/lyng-js/vm-dispatch-modernization-plan.md. The plan targets QuickJS interpreter parity on the V8 v7 suite by removing hot-loop Instruction materialization, eliminating wide-payload binary search, localizing frame/register state, refining hot opcode handlers, and later densifying bytecode. Phase 2b is scheduled with Phase 6, not immediately after Phase 2a. Keep Lyng JS no-unsafe policy intact.
acceptance: Implementation is broken into phase-sized child issues or PRs matching the persisted plan; Phase 1 byte-stream dispatch removes Instruction materialization from hot dispatch while preserving current wide/profiled compatibility; Phase 2a replaces binary-search wide_payload lookup with exact byte-offset presence metadata; Phase 3 localizes frame state and deletes VM-level PC APIs when helpers no longer need them; Phase 4/5 inline hot handlers and tighten register access without unsafe; Phase 6 lands density work and durable Wide/ExtraWide encoding with profiled-wrapper removal; phase reports, profiler artifacts, cargo asm snippets, Test262 evidence, runtime benches, density reports, and QuickJS comparisons are recorded under reports/js/lyng-js/.
notes: Important plan constraints: 2b measures installed-code footprint using actual pre-2b side metadata, not a fixed side-table byte assumption; ProfiledAbc/ProfiledAbx are transitional only; after 2b semantic opcode location and encoded length are self-describing from optional Wide/ExtraWide prefix plus semantic opcode; no Profiled prefix or prefix stacking; WidePayloadKind is replaced atomically by OperandWidthKind in 2b.
